insights: Pacing that sells. Something has to move on frame 1. Chat apps usually build the video thumbnail from an early frame, so a fade-in from black gives a black thumbnail that looks broken. In a 4-6 s opening, the hero action should land at about 60-75% of the way through. Give the card a 0.3-0.5 s 'breath' when it lands. Then cascade the card text in reading order over 2.5-3.5 s: Bismillah, hosts, names, event, date, time and venue, closing line. Hold the finished card for at least 6 s with only ambient motion. Aim for 14-22 s in total, plus an optional prelude of 5 s or less. Marketplace templates (VideoHive, Etsy, Canva) run 25-60 s only because they chain many scenes. Use one strong reveal, not a separate animation for every word.

Hierarchy. Names are the biggest element (13-15cqw script). The event title comes second (8-9cqw spaced caps). The date comes third in size but gets the strongest contrast and the longest still hold, because many guests watch with the sound off. Keep key text inside the central safe area, since WhatsApp and Instagram status UI covers roughly the top 12-14% and bottom 15-20% of a 9:16 frame. Detail text should be at least 4cqw (about 43 px at 1080 wide). Never run moving effects (petals, sparkles, smoke) over the names, the date, the QR code or sacred text. Mask those bands out of the .fall layer.

Event colour rules. Baraat: deep ruby, maroon, red sandstone or night tones with gold (Royal Ruby, Shahi Maroon, Velvet Maroon, Red Sandstone, Dusk Lahore, Firework Night). Walima: lighter and calmer, such as ivory, champagne, blush, sage, lilac, pistachio, or black-tie onyx and emerald (Ivory Blush, Champagne Onyx, Emerald Darbar, Lilac Silver, Pistachio Walima, Cotton Foil, Kashi Blue). Nikah: white, ivory, sage or midnight with gold calligraphy (Sage Nikah, Marble Gold, Midnight Gold, Cosmic Navy). Mehndi, Mayun and Dholki: marigold, mehndi green, hot pink, turquoise and truck-art brights (Mehndi Marigold, Basant Sky, Bangle Carnival, Truck Art Pop, Ajrak Indigo, Lollywood). Give every sample both a Baraat palette and a Walima palette, and switch between them automatically with the Event select. Example: Phoolon ki Larri uses Royal Ruby for Baraat and Ivory Blush for Walima.

Palette library. Roles are in the order bg/it/ef/cd/ink/ink2/acc/fl/lf. All were contrast-checked with a WCAG script: ink on cd is at least 11:1, ink2 on cd at least 5.2:1, and it on bg at least 6.9:1. Gold acc on light cards is only 2-3:1, so use acc for lines and ornaments, never for small text. Cultural guardrails for Pakistani Muslim weddings. Open with Arabic Bismillah, optionally followed by the common card line نحمده ونصلي على رسوله الكريم. Ar-Rum 30:21 and the du'a for newlyweds (بارك الله لكما وبارك عليكما وجمع بينكما في خير) are the usual blessings. Treat sacred text respectfully: only fade or draw it in, never bounce or spin it, never run petals or sparkles over it, give it a still hold, and verify the Arabic against quran.com. Avoid Hindu-specific imagery: Ganesha, kalash, om or swastika, mandap and fire rituals, aarti diya, rangoli, varmala garland exchange, sindoor, mangalsutra and elephant processions. Welcome motifs: Mughal arches, jaali, cusped mehrab, girih geometry, calligraphy, crescent and stars, lanterns, roses and motia, marigold (normal at Pakistani mehndis), henna, dholki, bangles, gota, truck art, ajrak, phulkari, kashi tiles, Badshahi Mosque, Lahore Fort and Shalimar. Ship faceless figures by default, a 'No figures' switch (geometric/floral only) for conservative families, and a design that reads perfectly with no music, since some families prefer nasheed, duff only or silence.

Pakistani card etiquette to build in. The Baraat and Rukhsati are hosted by the bride's family, so the bride's parents, the bride's name and the word daughter come first. The Walima is hosted by the groom's family, so the order flips. The dulha/dulhan pop-up prelude should follow a 'Whose side?' option (bride first for Baraat, groom first for Walima). Common extras: RSVP names with phone numbers; 'Muntazir' (those awaiting) and 'Dua-go' lists of relatives; programme timings (Baraat arrival, Nikah, dinner, Rukhsati); a bilingual Urdu/English layout; a QR or map pin. Urdu must never be split into per-letter spans, because that breaks Nastaliq joining. Reveal Urdu and Arabic with right-to-left clip wipes. The studio already falls back to a fade for Arabic-script names.

Polish details that separate premium from template. (1) Gold must look like metal: use a multi-stop gradient (#8C6A2B → #E9CF7A → #FFF4C8 → #B8913F → #9A7432) plus a moving specular glint at the hero moment and every 4-6 s on the hold. (2) Add 3-6% static noise or texture (SVG feTurbulence, rendered once) to large gradients, velvet, paper and sky, or H.264 will band them. (3) Moving strokes should be at least 0.3cqw (static hairlines at least 0.15cqw), or they shimmer at 1080p. (4) Use 3-5 parallax layers and one consistent light direction for shadows. (5) Easing: ease-out for entrances, ease-in for exits; overshoot or spring only for playful Mehndi designs; slow fades and draws for Nikah. (6) Stagger 40-120 ms; never move more than two things at once in the centre. (7) Use idle micro-motion on the hold (sway, glints, a 1-3% camera push-in) but keep the text block itself still. (8) The final frame must work as a static invite, because people screenshot it and html2mp4 saves it as the poster.

How html2mp4 renders, and what that means for the build. It pauses every entry in document.getAnimations() and seeks currentTime frame by frame, so all motion must be CSS animations or the Web Animations API. SVG SMIL (animate, animateMotion), requestAnimationFrame and canvas loops are not captured. Timers only line up in --virtual-time mode. Avoid CSS transitions, GIFs and video for choreography. Math.random is replaced by a seeded PRNG (seed 7, --seed flag), so random layouts made at setup are identical in every worker. Video length = the end of the last finite animation + the hold (or +0.5 s when the last animation is a full-card opaque fade). Infinite loops don't count, so make ambient loops infinite and make every one-shot end by about t0+4 s. The renderer waits for document.fonts.ready and for decode, but not for CSS background-image, so put photo backgrounds in . The stage is laid out at 360 CSS px (design_width) and scaled by deviceScaleFactor. Every form control is scanned as an option, so a 'Sample design'

CSS techniques and traps for this codebase. (a) .st has container-type:inline-size, so cqh does not refer to the card. It falls back to viewport units, which looks right in the full-frame video but wrong in the preview. Use cqw only and derive heights from --H:177.78cqw (9:16). (b) When drop, sway and exit animations all touch transform they overwrite each other. Use the individual translate, rotate and scale properties, nested wrappers, or animation-composition:add (Chromium 112+). (c) For springy pops use linear() easing, e.g. linear(0, 1.12 45%, .96 65%, 1.02 82%, 1) (Chromium 113+). (d) Register @property custom properties (<percentage>, <angle>) to animate mask radii, conic countdown sweeps and gradient positions. (e) The CSS d property morphs SVG paths when both paths have the same commands, which suits garlands and veils. (f) For flight paths use offset-path: path() with px coordinates in the 360×640 design box, and for the 340 px preview scale that motion box with a JS-set --k. Or use the no-motion-path trick: an outer wrapper animates X and an inner wrapper animates Y, with different easings. (g) For radial bursts, use a gravity-translate group containing a statically rotated wrapper, containing a dot that translates outward. (h) To sample glyph points (for particle initials), draw to an offscreen canvas only after document.fonts.ready. (i) Keep live card text out of 3D transforms: unfold a blank paper stand-in, then cross-fade to the real .card. (j) Use filters (blur, drop-shadow, displacement) only on small static regions, never animate filter attributes, and never use backdrop-filter at 4K.

Name collision to fix before adding the new palette roles. The stage CSS already defines --fl inside .st{...} as color-mix(in srgb,var(--ef) 95%,#000), and flapK uses it for the envelope flap. Setting the new floral role as an inline --fl with setProperty would override it and turn the envelope flap rose-red. Rename the internal variable (for example to --efl) or call the new role --flo. Derive new opening materials the same way the studio derives --eb, --el, --dr, --lt and --p2: color-mix() from the roles, never hard-coded colours, so every sample recolours with the event palette.

Integrating preludes without breaking the three existing openings. Add a Prelude select and a --p0 variable (prelude length, 0s by default). Change every opening-layer delay to calc(var(--p0) + Xs), for example .play.s-env .flap{animation:flapK .8s ease-in-out calc(var(--p0) + 3.05s) both}. In JS, t0() becomes P0[pre] + T0[style], so --t0, --te and the data-o detail delays shift automatically. The prelude layer is an opaque full-stage layer (z ≥ 9) that fades out over its last 0.4 s. Opening layers with fill-mode both sit in their first keyframe underneath it, which is fine. Keep .fdi (fade in from black) at 0 s, or better, start on the prelude's composed first frame so the thumbnail looks good.

Gallery UX for the Samples column. Store each sample as data: {id, name, events:[...], opening, prelude, border, pattern, names, details, falling, lanterns, sparkles, fonts, ornaments, palettes:{baraat:{...}, walima:{...}}}. Render tiles as live mini-stages frozen on their final frame by calling el.getAnimations({subtree:true}).forEach(a=>{a.pause(); a.currentTime=END}), because 40 simultaneous live animations would choke phones. Play a tile only on tap or hover (IntersectionObserver plus replay). Use filter chips for Baraat, Walima, Nikah, Mehndi, Modern and Heritage. 'Use this design' applies the whole recipe but keeps the client's names, dates and venue. Support a deep link (#sample=larri-baraat) so the client can send a link to one sample. Add a 'Surprise me' shuffle. Because html2mp4 scans selects, the same recipe list can drive renders: --set "Sample design=Phoolon ki Larri".

Keep the gallery visibly varied. No two neighbouring tiles should share more than one of these axes: background value (dark, mid, light), dominant hue (ruby, emerald, blue, gold, pastel, neon), motif family (architecture, floral, textile/craft, sky/night, folk-pop, modern-luxury, story/characters), and motion grammar (swing, part/curtain, unroll, unbox, assemble, dissolve, bloom, fly-through, stamp, draw, burst, zoom-through). The new openings below were chosen to cover every combination, and none reuses the envelope, door-swing or ring-draw mechanics of the existing three.

What buyers pay for, judging by Etsy, VideoHive and Fiverr listings: vertical 1080×1920 MP4s ready for WhatsApp; editable names, date, venue and RSVP; one design that covers Nikah, Walima and Mehndi variants; bilingual or Arabic fonts; gold-and-burgundy, floral, sage-green, turquoise and pink-and-gold styles; caricature or animated couples in their real outfit colours; RSVP, countdown and map extras. Prices run from about $5 to $50, so polish and personalisation are the differentiators. In WeddingWire India's 2024-25 survey, 57% of respondents announced their wedding on WhatsApp, and chat-style, caricature and minimal-initials invites are all named trends. Recommend sending as a Document on WhatsApp to avoid recompression.

concepts.name: Phoolon ki Larri (Jasmine & Rose Strand Curtain)
storyboard: 0.0-0.5s: Deep stage with a soft vignette; a warm glow starts building behind the centre (0→35%).

0.3-1.3s: 15 floral strands drop in from above the top edge, centre strand first and then outward (60 ms stagger). They alternate between chains of white motia buds and chains of red rose heads with tiny leaves, each ending in a gold bell or gota tassel. Springy landing with an 8% overshoot.
1.3-2.3s: The curtain breathes, each strand swaying ±2° on its own phase. A small velvet plaque hangs mid-curtain: 'We cordially invite you to the' / BARAAT (script) / 'of Ayesha & Hamza'.
2.3-2.6s: The plaque rises and fades; the backlight brightens until the card's arch silhouette shows through the gaps.
2.6-3.9s: The curtain is drawn aside from the middle. Strands slide outward (centre strands travel furthest), tilt 6-10° and bunch at both edges (scaleX .55). Two gold tie-back bows pop on at 3.5s.
3.9-4.6s: The card settles from scale .95 to 1 with a soft bloom; a few jasmine buds drop and fall; the bunched strands stay as side garlands framing the card.
4.6s: t0. The Bismillah, names and details cascade in.
concepts.why_it_wins: Floral-strand curtains are the signature backdrop of Pakistani mehndi and baraat stages and echo the groom's sehra, so guests recognise them instantly. The soft, organic parting feels romantic and is clearly different from the rigid palace doors.
concepts.build_notes: key 'larri', T0 4.6, DEF {b:'garland', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:false, spk:true}. Layer .larri-l (z 8) sits above .card. JS (setup only) creates 15 strands with --c = signed index from the centre (-7..7) and a seeded length of 58-78% of stage height (use --H:177.78cqw, since cqh is unreliable here). Each strand is three nested wrappers so no animation overwrites another: .sw-out (partK: translateX c*6.5cqw, rotate c*1.2deg, scaleX .55 at the edges), .sw-drop (dropK: translateY -110% → 0 with linear(0, 1.08 55%, .97 75%, 1)), and .sw-sway (swayK: rotate -2deg↔2deg, 1.7s ease-in-out infinite alternate, negative phase delay per strand). All use transform-origin 50% 0. Strand art: a 0.35cqw gold thread line plus <use href='#bud'>/<use href='#rose'> every 4.2cqw (symbols defined once). Compute delays in JS: drop = p0+.3+|c|*.06, part = p0+2.6+(7-|c|)*.03. The backlight is a radial-gradient div in color-mix(in srgb, var(--acc) 60%, #fff) with opacity keyframes. Tie-back bows use popK at 3.5s. The card gets fadeS at 3.9s. Roles: ef = jasmine buds, fl = roses, lf = leaves, acc = thread/bells/bows. About 200 <use> nodes, which is cheap at 4K.

concepts.name: Gulab Khilna (Rose Bloom Dive)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: Soft vignette. A closed rosebud rises from the bottom while its stem draws upward and two leaves unfurl from their bases.

0.8-2.3s: The bud opens in four rings of petals, inner to outer, 0.25 s apart. Each petal tilts outward from a closed pose (scaleY .5, rotate -15°) to full bloom, and the centre deepens in colour. A dew glint twinkles at 2.1s.
2.3-3.2s: The camera dives into the bloom: the rose scales ×1→×5 around its heart while the outer petals fly radially past the frame.
3.2-4.2s: The card opens from the rose's heart as a feathered circle (mask radius 0%→150%), while 8-10 loose petals tumble across it.
4.2s: t0. The names write in by hand; petals keep falling softly.
concepts.why_it_wins: Rose petals are showered on the baraat and decorate every stage. One rose opening into the invitation is universally romantic and makes a strong thumbnail, and the dive into the flower feels cinematic rather than templated.
concepts.build_notes: key 'rose', T0 4.2, DEF {b:'corner', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:false, spk:true}. One SVG (viewBox 0 0 100 100) with 22 petal paths in 4 rings; JS sets --a (angle), --ring and a delay for each petal. Structure per petal: rotated by var(--a) (transform-origin 50px 50px) > (flyK: translateY 0 → -60, which moves along the petal's own axis because it sits inside the rotated group) > (openK: scale(.35,.5) rotate(-15deg) → none; transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: 50% 100%, the petal base). Petal fill is a linear-gradient from color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 75%, #000) at the base to color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 80%, #fff) at the lip, with a thin lighter rim stroke. Stem and leaves use pathLength=1 + drawK; leaves scale from their base. The dive is a wrapper scale 1→5 with cubic-bezier(.5,0,.9,.4). Card reveal: @property --m {syntax:''; inherits:false; initial-value:0%}; .card{mask-image: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 46%, #000 var(--m), transparent calc(var(--m) + 12%))}, also -webkit-mask-image, animating --m 0%→150%. Optional photo background: the Unsplash dark-roses photo-1518709779341 as an at 35% under a vignette.

concepts.name: Shahi Farman (Royal Scroll Unroll)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A rolled parchment scroll with turned gold finials swings down from the top on a red silk cord and settles (pendulum ±8°→0).
1.0-1.6s: The red wax seal stamped with the couple's initials pulses, then cracks along a jagged line; its halves drop away with a spin and the cord slides off.

1.6-3.3s: The scroll unrolls downward. The top roller stays at 8% height while the bottom roller travels to 93%, spinning as it rolls. The parchment revealed behind it is the card itself, and its double border draws in as it appears.
3.3-3.8s: The bottom roller overshoots by 1% and settles; small puffs of gold dust come off both roller ends.
3.6-4.2s: t0 at 3.6s. Text fades up line by line in a formal cadence (Bismillah, hosts, names, event, date) while the border finishes drawing.
concepts.why_it_wins: Scroll cards ('farman') descend from royal Mughal announcements and are a much-loved premium print format. Because the card itself is what gets revealed, it reads clearly on a phone and feels regal without being busy.
concepts.build_notes: key 'farman', T0 3.6, DEF {b:'double', n:'letter', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:false}. The .card is the parchment. Animate its clip-path from inset(0 0 92% 0) to inset(0 0 7% 0) over 1.7s with cubic-bezier(.45,.05,.25,1), starting at p0+1.6s. The bottom roller div animates top 8%→93% with the same duration and easing, so the edge stays glued to it. Rollers: width 94%, height 4.5cqw, a gold linear-gradient (#8C6A2B, #E9CF7A, #B8913F) plus repeating-linear-gradient stripes. The spinning illusion is a background-position-y animation over the same 1.7s. Finials are circles at the roller ends. Pendulum: wrapper rotate keyframes 8deg→-5→3→0 with transform-origin 50% -40%. Seal: an SVG circle with a scalloped edge in var(--fl) plus the .xin initials. The crack is two clipPath halves animating translate and rotate with ease-in, for gravity. Parchment texture: a static SVG feTurbulence (baseFrequency .8, numOctaves 3) multiplied at 6-8%; never animate filters. Deckled left and right edges: a clip-path polygon generated in JS with seeded jitter. Roles: cd/ef = parchment and shading, fl = cord and seal, acc = finials and border.

concepts.name: Mithai ka Dibba (Gifted Sweet-Box Unboxing)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: Top-down view of a cream tabletop. An ornate square box slides up into the centre with a soft shadow: velvet lid, gota-kinari border and a gold 'A & H' medallion. Two brass bells on the ribbon tails jingle.
0.8-1.5s: The gota ribbon bow unties. The loops shrink and spin away, and the crossing ribbons retract to the box edges.
1.5-2.4s: The lid lifts toward the camera (scale 1→1.18, its shadow spreading and softening), then glides off to the upper right with a 12° turn.
2.4-3.2s: Inside, a bed of rose petals and silver-vark sweets (diamond barfi, round ladoo) surrounds a folded card. A warm glow rises and the vark glints.
3.2-4.6s: The folded card lifts, its top flap swings open 180°, and it scales up to fill the frame as the box sinks away.
concepts.why_it_wins: In Pakistan the card often arrives with a box of mithai or dry fruit, so an unboxing reveal mirrors the real ritual. Unboxing is satisfying to watch and gives a luxurious, gift-like first impression.
concepts.build_notes: key 'dibba', T0 4.6, DEF {b:'corner', n:'slide', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:false, spk:true}. Shoot it top-down so no 3D box is needed: the lid lift is scale + translate + a box-shadow that grows and softens (0 1cqw 2cqw → 0 6cqw 9cqw rgba(0,0,0,.35)). Box: a div with a velvet radial-gradient (var(--fl) at the centre, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 65%, #000) at the edges) and a gota border made of repeating-radial-gradient scallops in var(--acc). Ribbon: two crossing strips (scaleX/scaleY to 0 toward the edges) and a bow of two ellipses (scale 0 + rotate 90deg). Sweets: about 10 <use> symbols with a silver gradient (#E9EDF2→#B8C0CA) and a pistachio dot in var(--lf). Card unfold: a blank paper element inside a parent with perspective:140cqw; its top half rotates rotateX(-180deg→0) with backface-visibility:hidden. At p0+4.3s, cross-fade to the real .card so live text never sits inside a 3D transform and stays crisp. Roles: fl = velvet, acc = gota and medallion, ef = box interior and paper, lf = pistachio.

Baraat · Shahi Maroon #2A0A12/#F6E3C3/#F3E3C8/#FFF8EE/#3A1016/#8C1D2C/#C9A04E/#B3203A/#2F6B4F. Tabletop: color-mix(in srgb, var(--ef) 80%, #fff).

concepts.name: Jaali ki Roshni (Marble Lattice Light Dissolve)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A full-screen white-marble jaali (hexagon-and-star lattice) stands in darkness. Light grows behind it: the holes glow from dim amber to bright gold and soft god-rays fall diagonally.
1.0-2.0s: The couple's initials glow through the central rosette like a stencil, with a one-line intro beneath.
2.0-3.6s: The lattice dissolves from the centre outward, ring after ring (60 ms per ring): each cell shrinks, turns 45° and fades, uncovering the card.
3.6-4.0s: The outermost ring of cells stays as a carved frame and softens to 40% opacity.
4.0s: t0. Text fades in with a slow, reverent rhythm.
concepts.why_it_wins: Jaali is the most recognisable detail of Mughal architecture, and light through stone feels serene and spiritual, which is ideal for a Nikah. The cell-by-cell dissolve is mesmerising and unlike any door or envelope.
concepts.build_notes: key 'jaali', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'arch', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:false}. JS lays out an 8×14 grid of <use href='#cell'> at 12.5cqw pitch. Each cell is a square with a star-shaped hole (fill-rule:evenodd) plus an inner bevel path in color-mix(in srgb, var(--ef) 85%, #000). For each cell compute ring = Chebyshev distance from the centre and set animation-delay = p0 + 2.0 + ring*0.06 s. Dissolve keyframes: scale 1→0, rotate 0→45deg, opacity 1→0, ease-in, with transform-box: fill-box and transform-origin: center. Cells with ring ≥ 6 skip the dissolve and become the frame. Light comes from two layers behind the jaali: a radial-gradient (acc→transparent) with an opacity ramp, and a conic-gradient ray layer at 25% opacity with mix-blend-mode: screen that rotates 4° over 4s. Stencil initials: an SVG <mask> with the initials as black text cuts the rosette, so the glow shows through. Roles: ef = marble, acc = glow and rays, bg = darkness.
concepts.palette_idea: Nikah/Walima · Marble Gold #2E2418/#F4EAD6/#F4F1EA/#FFFBF3/#2E2418/#7E5F26/#B8913F/#D9A3A3/#6E8F7A (bg/it/ef/cd/ink/ink2/acc/fl/lf). Baraat · Red Sandstone #3C1D14/#F6E3C3/#F2E2CB/#FFF7EA/#3C1D14/#9A3D29/#D4A95C/#C8434F/#5E7A55, with ef set to #B5533C for a sandstone jaali.

concepts.name: Kashi Kari (Wazir Khan Tile Mosaic)
storyboard: 0.0-1.8s: Glazed tiles flip into place in a diagonal wave from top-left to bottom-right, each landing with a tiny bounce, until a full-screen panel of cobalt, turquoise, ochre and white floral and geometric tiles is built.
1.8-2.5s: A glossy glaze highlight sweeps diagonally across the panel. A central cartouche reads 'Shaadi Mubarak' in Nastaliq, with the couple's names beneath.
2.5-3.8s: Starting from the centre, tiles flip away edge-on in an expanding diamond, uncovering the card. The outer two rows stay to frame it as a tile border.
3.8-4.2s: t0 at 3.8s. A glint runs along the remaining border tiles as the text begins.
concepts.why_it_wins: This is pure Lahore heritage: the Wazir Khan Mosque's tile cladding is described as the most extensive of any Mughal building. The cobalt and turquoise palette stands out among maroon-and-gold invites, and the tile assembly is satisfying and rhythmic.
concepts.build_notes: key 'kashi', T0 3.8, DEF {b:'kashi' (new tile border; fallback 'double'), n:'letter', d:'wipe', f:'none', lan:false, spk:true}. JS builds a 6×11 grid of .tile divs. Each tile picks (seeded) one of 4 designs drawn as small SVG data-URIs in palette colours: rosette, 8-point star, guldasta vase, cypress. Rebuild the data-URIs when the colours change. Parent perspective: 220cqw; tiles use backface-visibility hidden. Assembly: rotateY(180deg)→0 with delay (col+row)*45ms and a linear() overshoot. Exit: rotateY(0→-90deg) plus opacity, with delay (|col-cx|+|row-cy|)*55ms; rows 0 and 10 and columns 0 and 5 skip the exit. Gloss: a skewed linear-gradient band (rgba(255,255,255,.45)) translating -130%→130% with mix-blend-mode: soft-light. The cartouche is a separate centred element (Gulzar or Noto Nastaliq Urdu) that fades out at 2.5s. Roles: ink2 = cobalt, lf = turquoise, acc = ochre, ef = tile white, fl = terracotta accent.

concepts.name: Girih Kaleidoscope (Islamic Star Unfolding)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: A lapis-night background. An 8-point star draws itself in gold at the centre, then rings of stars, crosses and hexagons draw outward in staggered strokes, forming a girih rosette that fills the screen.
1.2-2.4s: The rings counter-rotate slowly (inner clockwise, outer anticlockwise) as turquoise and lapis fills fade in, like a living kaleidoscope. The intro line sits inside the central star.
2.4-3.4s: The central star grows to fill the frame and its 8 kite-shaped petals fold outward like a flower, revealing the card through a star-shaped window.
3.4-4.0s: The star window expands past the edges; faint star outlines linger in the card corners.
concepts.why_it_wins: Islamic geometry signals faith and elegance without any figures, so it suits conservative families. The self-drawing pattern is hypnotic and, being pure vector, stays razor-sharp at 4K.
concepts.build_notes: key 'girih', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'corner', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Generate the geometry in JS at setup: {8/3} star points at radius r, and rings at r×[1, 2.2, 3.6, 5.2] with 8/16/24/32 repeats. Every path gets pathLength=1 and drawK with staggered --d. Rotation: each ring sits in <g class='rg'> with transform-box: view-box and transform-origin: 50% 50%; spin keyframes of ±12deg run over the scene and are finite. Fills: fill-opacity 0→.85 after each stroke completes. Star window: .card uses clip-path: polygon() with the 16 points of an 8-point star. Write two keyframe stops (scale .05 and 3; coordinates outside 0-100% are fine) into a <style> at setup. Polygon interpolation works because the point count is identical. Petal fold: 8 kite paths scaleY(1→0) with transform-origin at their outer tips (transform-box: fill-box). Roles: acc = gold lines, lf = turquoise, ink2/bg = lapis.

concepts.name: Mor Pankh (Peacock Fan Reveal)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A stylised Mughal-miniature peacock steps in from the left to bottom-centre with a gentle head bob.

0.8-2.2s: Its train lifts and fans open. 24 feathers rotate from folded to their fan angles (−80°…80°), centre first, then outward. Each eyespot shimmers turquoise and gold as it settles, and the fan gives a quick quiver at 2.0s.
2.2-3.0s: The fan glows into a radiant halo, with the couple's initials appearing at its centre.
3.0-4.2s: The camera rises into the fan and the feathers sweep outward past the frame, revealing the card. The bird fades, and two feathers remain as corner ornaments.
concepts.why_it_wins: Peacocks were favourites of Mughal painters and are one of the most common subjects in Pakistani truck art. The jewel-tone fan is a show-stopping, very shareable moment.
concepts.build_notes: key 'mor', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'corner', n:'slide', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. One feather <symbol> is reused by 24 <use> elements, each with a --a target angle and a delay. The symbol has a shaft path, a barb fan drawn as a gradient-filled teardrop with fine hairline strokes, and an eyespot of nested ellipses (lf, ink2-blue, an acc ring, a dark pupil). The group's transform-origin is the rump point in viewBox units (transform-box: view-box; transform-origin: 180px 520px). Opening: rotate var(--a0) (near 0) → var(--a) with cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). The quiver is a short rotate ±1.2deg keyframe at 2.0s on a separate inner group. Bird body: a flat stylised silhouette with a #1E5BA8 → lf neck gradient and a crest of 3 dots; the walk is translate plus a steps(4) head bob. Sweep-out: each feather goes to scale 3, rotates ±20deg and fades. Keep it flat in the miniature style, because realistic SVG peacocks look cheap.

concepts.name: Badshahi Chaand (Moonrise over Badshahi Mosque)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: A dusk sky gradient (indigo → plum → apricot horizon) above the silhouette of the Badshahi Mosque (three domes, four minarets) along the lower third. Stars twinkle in and tiny city lights flicker on.
1.2-2.4s: A thin crescent rises behind the central dome with a soft halo, and a flock of pigeons crosses the sky.
2.4-3.2s: The crescent fills into a full moon as its shadow slides away, a symbol of completion. 'With the blessings of Allah…' appears beneath it.
3.2-4.4s: The moon swells into a luminous circle that washes the screen with light, and the card appears inside the glow. The mosque silhouette sinks to become a skyline footer on the card.
concepts.why_it_wins: A Lahore landmark plus the crescent is instantly local and unmistakably Muslim. It reads like a film poster and works beautifully for night baraats.
concepts.build_notes: key 'chaand', T0 4.3, DEF {b:'arch', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:true, spk:true}. Silhouette: one SVG path (domes from arcs, minarets as rectangles with chhatri caps) filled with color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 70%, #000). Sky: a linear-gradient from var(--bg) through color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 60%, var(--fl)) to color-mix(in srgb, var(--acc) 70%, #fff), plus 4% static noise to prevent H.264 banding. Stars: 60 seeded dots with twK infinite (infinite loops don't lengthen the video). Moon: an SVG circle with a holding a black circle that translates away, turning the crescent into a full moon. The halo is a radial-gradient with mix-blend-mode: screen. Swell: the moon group scales 1→14 (transform-origin at the moon's centre) under a white-gold overlay opacity, and the card fades in beneath it. Birds: small V paths flapping via scaleY steps(2) infinite, flying via translate. Optional photo version: an of Unsplash photo-1758714144057 (Badshahi at sunset) or photo-1531804308561 (minaret under stars, already portrait) with a 55% bg-colour gradient overlay. Use , not a CSS background, so html2mp4 waits for it.

concepts.name: Shaadi Wala Ghar (The Wedding House Lights Up)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A night street with a flat-illustrated Lahori haveli facade (jharokha balconies, an arched gate, wooden shutters), all dark.

0.8-2.4s: Cascading strings of fairy lights switch on from the roof downward in waves, the way Pakistani families light up the shaadi house: warm white and gold with a few red and green bulbs. A 'Shaadi Mubarak' marquee over the gate lights up letter by letter.
2.4-3.2s: The central jharokha's shutters swing open, warm light floods out, and the intro line glows in the window.
3.2-4.6s: The camera dollies into the window (scene scale 1→5 around it). The window arch frames the card, which fills the screen, while the light strings stay behind as twinkling bokeh.
concepts.why_it_wins: Every Pakistani knows the lit-up 'shaadi wala ghar', so the scene is pure nostalgia and joy, perfect for dholki and mehndi nights. The push-in through the window is cinematic.
concepts.build_notes: key 'ghar', T0 4.5, DEF {b:'double', n:'letter', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:true, spk:true}. Facade: flat SVG shapes in color-mix tints of bg; no gradients needed. Lights: draw about 20 vertical strings × 18 bulbs once as an SVG pattern of circles. Switch them on with a mask, linear-gradient(to bottom, #000 var(--y), transparent calc(var(--y) + 8%)), where @property --y animates 0%→100%; that is one animation instead of 360 elements. A second, sparse layer of seeded bulbs runs twK infinite for twinkle. Marquee: letters as spans with staggered opacity steps. Shutters: two small divs rotating ±105deg on Y, with perspective on the window. Dolly: wrap the scene in .ghar-sc with transform-origin at the window centre and scale 1→5 (ease-in, cubic-bezier(.6,0,.9,.5)). At 4.2s the .card starts at scale(.2) placed at the window and grows to 1, zoomK-style. Bulb colours: #FFE3A3, #FFF1C9, var(--fl), var(--lf). Optional photo: the Unsplash string-light bokeh photo-1544438369-a34666f8ff77, blurred behind the card.

concepts.name: Patang Bazi (Basant Kite Delivery)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A bright spring sky (mustard-gold to sky blue) over old-Lahore rooftops along the bottom. Four kites in pink, green, purple and mustard bob and drift.
1.0-2.2s: One large kite carrying the couple's initials swoops toward the camera on a curved path, its tail ribbons fluttering, while the other kites drift aside.
2.2-3.0s: A playful 'bo-kata!' beat: the string snaps and retracts, and the kite tumbles once and flips to face the camera, filling the frame.
3.0-4.2s: The kite's diamond expands into the card (a diamond clip that grows past the edges). Its tail ribbons become ribbons on the card, and mustard-flower (sarson) petals drift down.
concepts.why_it_wins: Basant is Lahore's own festival, and it returned in February 2026 after a 19-year ban, so the kite is a fresh, joyful and very local hook. It is bright, playful and nothing like the usual gold-and-maroon invite. Keep it whimsical: the festival remains controversial because of kite-string injuries, so never show glass-coated string.
concepts.build_notes: key 'patang', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'single', n:'slide', d:'slide', f:'petal' (petals recoloured sarson yellow), lan:false, spk:false}. Kite: an SVG diamond with cross spars and a tail of 3 bows; the bows swing with an infinite rotate. Swoop: either use offset-path: path('M -40 520 C 80 380, 300 420, 180 300') with offset-distance 0→100% and offset-rotate: auto 45deg, or the no-motion-path trick (an outer wrapper translates X with ease-in-out, an inner wrapper translates Y with ease-out, giving a smooth curve). The offset-path coordinates are in the 360×640 design space html2mp4 lays out at; for the 340px preview, scale a 360×640 motion box by a JS-set --k. String: a line from the kite to off-screen bottom; the snap is scaleY(1→0) toward the bottom. Diamond reveal: .card clip-path: polygon(50% a, b 50%, 50% c, d 50%) keyframes, from a small diamond to one far outside the box. Rooftops: flat silhouettes with water tanks and a minaret.

concepts.name: Kabootar ka Paigham (Doves Bring the Garland)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: Misty dawn. Two white doves fly in from left and right, carrying between their beaks a strand of jasmine and roses with a small gold heart locket at its centre.
1.2-2.0s: They meet at top-centre and hover; the garland sags into a gentle curve and the locket swings.
2.0-2.8s: The locket opens (its two halves swing apart) with a sparkle burst, and the initials glow inside.
2.8-4.0s: The doves rise and exit through the top corners. The garland drops and settles as the card's top border, while the card blooms out from the locket point in a soft radial reveal.
concepts.why_it_wins: Gentle, pure and universal: messenger birds are a classic romantic image in Urdu poetry and film. Watching the garland fall into place as the border is a satisfying 'everything fits' moment.
concepts.build_notes: key 'kabootar', T0 3.9, DEF {b:'garland', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:false, spk:true}. Dove: three wing poses as separate <g> elements in one SVG, shown in turn by an opacity keyframe with steps(3) on a 0.36s infinite loop (no SMIL); the body bobs via translate. Flight paths: nested translate wrappers (as in 'patang') or offset-path. Garland: an SVG path whose shape morphs via the CSS d property from a taut line to a sag curve (Chromium animates d: path(...) when both paths have the same commands). Beads come from stroke-dasharray: 0 3.2 with stroke-linecap: round, in two offset layers (fl roses, ef jasmine). Locket: two heart halves rotating ±120deg on Y in a perspective parent. Finish: the garland path cross-fades into the existing .b-g garland border, so the border is the real one. Reveal: a radial mask from the locket position, using the same @property --m trick as 'rose'.

concepts.name: Dupatta Unveil (Bridal Veil Lift)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: The card sits blurred beneath a sheer red net dupatta with a gold gota border and scattered sequins that twinkle. The veil breathes with a slow wave.
1.0-2.0s: Intro text sits on the veil: 'Ek naya safar…' / 'We invite you to the Baraat'. Tassels (latkan) at the corners swing.
2.0-3.6s: The veil lifts from its bottom edge and floats off toward the top-right with a flowing ripple. The sequins catch the light as it moves, and the card's blur clears (6px → 0).
3.6-4.2s: The veil exits and a matching gota border draws onto the card.
concepts.why_it_wins: The bride's red dupatta is the emotional heart of a Pakistani baraat. This reveal is literally an unveiling, tender and dramatic, and the sheer fabric looks luxurious in motion.
concepts.build_notes: key 'dupatta', T0 3.8, DEF {b:'gota' (new) or 'double', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Veil: a div with an SVG net pattern (tiny diamonds) in var(--fl) at 55% opacity, plus a gota edge (acc stripes from repeating-linear-gradient with a scalloped mask). Flowing bottom edge: an inner SVG with a sine-like path animated via the CSS d property (3 keyframes, same command count). Lift: keyframes on translate, rotate and skewX (e.g. 0 → translate(35%,-70%) rotate(12deg) skewX(-8deg) → off-screen) with cubic-bezier(.55,.05,.35,1). Sequins: 25 seeded dots inside the veil with twK. Card blur: filter: blur(1.6cqw) → 0 on the .card wrapper, only during 2.0-3.6s. Filters are costly at 4K, so keep that window short and never animate backdrop-filter. Tassels: a small SVG with the sw sway.

concepts.name: Rang Bhari (Watercolour Ink Bloom)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: Cold-press watercolour paper texture with a faint pencil sketch of an arch.
0.6-2.4s: Drops of pigment (blush, sage, gold) fall and bloom outward with organic, darker-rimmed edges; the blooms overlap and mix.
2.4-3.6s: The blooms spread to cover the frame and a floral illustration emerges inside the colour. A final large wash of the card colour clears a calm centre for the text.
3.6-4.2s: Gold-leaf flecks shimmer on the blooms.
concepts.why_it_wins: Modern couples love a hand-painted look that is soft, artistic and calm. A bloom that seems to be painted live feels bespoke rather than templated.
concepts.build_notes: key 'bloom', T0 3.8, DEF {b:'single', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'none', lan:false, spk:true}. Each bloom is an SVG circle with a radial-gradient fill (lighter centre, darker rim, mimicking watercolour edge darkening). All blooms pass through ONE shared static filter (feTurbulence baseFrequency .02, numOctaves 2 → feDisplacementMap scale 18) for ragged edges. Animate r via CSS (r is a CSS property in Chromium) or transform scale, never the filter itself: CSS cannot keyframe filter attributes, and html2mp4 cannot seek SMIL. Use mix-blend-mode: multiply. Card reveal: an SVG <mask> reusing the same bloom group, so the card appears exactly where the colour spreads. For 4K speed, limit it to 8 blooms and set the filter region tightly (x/y/width/height). Gold flecks: 30 small polygons with a gold gradient and twK.

concepts.name: Shalimar Bagh (Paper-Cut Mughal Garden Fly-Through)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: Layered paper-cut scenery pops up from the bottom like a pop-up book: a sky with sun, the marble pavilion with cusped arches, cypress trees left and right, the central water channel with fountains, and rose beds in front. Each layer casts a soft paper shadow.
1.2-2.4s: The fountains play (dashed water jets), petals drift, and the layers drift at different speeds as the camera slowly pushes in.
2.4-3.8s: The camera flies through the central arch. Foreground layers scale up fast and slide off the sides, and the arch grows to fill the screen with the card inside it.
3.8-4.4s: The arch outline remains as the card's arch border.
concepts.why_it_wins: Lahore's Shalimar Gardens are a UNESCO-listed Mughal garden. Layered paper-cut depth looks handcrafted and premium, and the fly-through gives real cinematic depth on a phone.
concepts.build_notes: key 'shalimar', T0 4.2, DEF {b:'arch', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:false, spk:false}. Six absolutely positioned SVG layers, back to front: sky, pavilion, back cypress, channel and fountains, front cypress, rose bed. Each has filter: drop-shadow(0 .6cqw .8cqw rgba(0,0,0,.22)); static drop-shadows are fine. Pop-up: rotateX(-90deg→0) with transform-origin bottom, parent perspective 260cqw, staggered 0.12s. Drift: translateX by depth (front ±3cqw). Fly-through: each layer scales from 1 to 1+depth*2.2 with transform-origin at the arch centre (50% 52%) and ease-in; the front layers also translate outward and fade. Fountains: vertical paths with stroke-dasharray and an infinite dashoffset loop. Make the final arch path identical to the .b-arch border path so the hand-off is seamless. Reference photo for colours and composition: the Unsplash Naulakha pavilion, photo-1792332446550.

concepts.name: Pop-up Kitaab (Mughal Storybook)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A closed hardbound book rests on a dark table. Its tooled leather cover is maroon with gold tooling and a central medallion bearing the initials.
0.8-1.8s: The cover swings open on its left hinge, revealing the first spread.
1.8-3.0s: A pop-up scene rises from the gutter in three layers: a Mughal palace arch, then the groom on a white horse on the left page and the bride's doli on the right.
3.0-4.4s: The camera tilts and zooms into the pop-up arch; its opening frames the card, which expands to full screen.
concepts.why_it_wins: Storybook romance with tactile 3D; 3D book invitations are a strong trend on template marketplaces. It tells the couple's story in one beat.
concepts.build_notes: key 'kitaab', T0 4.3, DEF {b:'arch', n:'letter', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Book: the front cover has two faces (outside leather, inside endpaper) with backface-visibility hidden. It rotates rotateY(0→-180deg) around the left edge inside a parent with perspective:200cqw. concepts.name: Mehndi mein Naam (Henna Draws Itself, Find the Groom's Name)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: A warm marigold background. Two open palms (flat, stylised) rise into frame side by side.
0.6-2.6s: Henna patterns draw themselves on both palms in henna-brown: vines, paisleys (buta), nets and fingertip caps, with dots popping at the ends of the strokes.
2.6-3.4s: A magnifying-glass circle glides over the right palm and stops. Inside the lens, the groom's name, hidden in the pattern, appears enlarged, with a playful sparkle and 'Mil gaya!'.
3.4-4.6s: The palms part to the sides like a book opening, and the card rises between them. Henna vines extend from the palms to form its border.

concepts.build_notes: key 'mehndi', T0 4.5, DEF {b:'corner', n:'hand', d:'slide', f:'petal' (marigold petals), lan:false, spk:true}. Hands: one simplified palm-and-fingers path, mirrored for the left hand, filled with a warm neutral skin tone (#E3B48C, with 2 alternates in the UI). Henna: 40-60 short paths with pathLength=1 and drawK, staggered by JS via --d. Strokes use color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 70%, #7A2E12) with round caps; dots appear via popK. Hidden name: an SVG <text> in a script font (~1.6cqw) placed along the palm. The lens is a circular clipPath containing a <use> of the hand group scaled ×2.5 around the lens centre, plus a ring and handle; the lens group translates along 2 keyframes. Parting: each hand translates ±60cqw on X and rotates ±8deg (ease-in-out). Henna border: the existing corner flourishes, recoloured henna brown.

concepts.name: Jhoomar (Crystal Chandelier)
storyboard: 0.0-1.4s: A dark ballroom with a faint damask wall. A crystal chandelier descends on its chain, swaying gently, its crystals catching points of light.
1.4-2.4s: The bulbs ignite tier by tier from the bottom; the warm glow expands with soft lens rays.
2.4-3.2s: The light swells into a white-gold bloom that fills the screen.
3.2-4.2s: The bloom recedes to reveal the card. The chandelier, now small, hangs at the top of the card as an ornament with a gentle crystal twinkle.
concepts.why_it_wins: Most walimas are held in hotel ballrooms or marquees, and the chandelier is shorthand for luxury. The flash-to-card transition is clean and elegant.
concepts.build_notes: key 'jhoomar', T0 3.6, DEF {b:'double', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Chandelier SVG: 3 tiers of arcs with hanging crystal drops (one diamond <symbol> reused about 60 times). Candle bulbs are radial-gradient circles, which are cheaper and sharper than feGaussianBlur. Descent: translateY(-100%) → 0 with a spring linear(); sway: a damped rotate (3, -2, 1, 0 deg) around the chain top. Ignite: bulb opacity 0→1, staggered by tier. Bloom: a full-stage radial-gradient overlay (#FFF6E0 → transparent) with mix-blend-mode: screen, opacity 0→.92→0. After the bloom, the chandelier group scales to .32 and moves to the card's top centre, where it stays as the ornament with an infinite twinkle. 1.6-2.4s: Red velvet curtains under a spotlight; marquee bulbs chase around a 'NOW SHOWING' sign.

2.4-3.6s: The curtains part and lift into swags, revealing a hand-painted retro film poster. The couple appear as faceless illustrated leads under the title 'Hamza weds Ayesha' in bold Urdu and English lettering, with the tagline 'A Love Story — Releasing 12.12.2026'.

Countdown: @property --a {syntax:'<angle>'}, and a circle with conic-gradient(from 0deg, rgba(255,255,255,.22) var(--a), transparent 0) sweeping 0→360deg once per number. The numbers 3/2/1 swap via opacity keyframes with steps. Grain: a static SVG noise tile whose background-position jumps with steps(8) infinite, for deterministic flicker; scratches are 2 thin lines with jumpy translate steps. Curtains: two divs with repeating-linear-gradient folds. Parting is scaleX(1→.28) from the outer edges, plus skewY(4deg) and translateY(-6%) for the swags. Marquee bulbs: dots with staggered blink steps. storyboard: 0.0-1.6s: In old-film style, a newspaper spins in from the distance, making three full turns while scaling 0.05→1, with ghost trails.

1.6-2.8s: It lands with a thump and a small bounce. The masthead reads 'The Lahore Shaadi Times', the headline 'BREAKING: Hamza & Ayesha to tie the knot!', with the date in the sub-head. A red 'EXCLUSIVE' stamp thuds on.

concepts.name: Aarsi Mushaf (The First-Glance Mirror)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: An ornate silver hand-mirror with a filigree frame floats in against a draped red dupatta; its glass is fogged.
1.0-2.0s: A soft light sweep clears the fog, revealing the couple's names written mirror-reversed in the glass: the moment the couple first see each other in the mirror.
2.0-2.8s: The mirror turns around 180° so the names read correctly, with a sparkle along the filigree.
2.8-4.2s: The mirror's oval grows to fill the screen, revealing the card; the filigree becomes an oval frame around the names.

Mirror: an SVG oval with a filigree ring (one small scroll motif repeated 24× around the ellipse via rotate) and a handle below. The glass is a silver linear-gradient (#E6E9EE→#9AA3AD). Fog: a white radial-gradient blob layer, cleared by a moving mask (@property --p animates the mask gradient position 0%→100%). Mirrored names: a text group with scaleX(-1). Turnaround: the mirror group rotates rotateY(0→180deg) in a perspective parent with two faces (front: mirrored names, back: correct names) and backface-visibility hidden. concepts.name: Fanoos Udaan (Sky-Lantern Release)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: A night sky over a garden silhouette. Dozens of paper lanterns rise from below at different speeds, flickering warm.
1.2-2.4s: One larger lantern drifts toward the camera, the couple's initials cut into its paper like a silhouette.
2.4-3.4s: It comes so close that its glow fills the screen with warm amber.
3.4-4.2s: The glow settles into the card's background while small lanterns keep rising behind the card edges.

JS generates 30 lanterns with seeded size (4-9cqw), x position (0-100%) and duration (5-9s), plus negative delays so the sky is already full at frame 1. riseK translates each one from 110% of stage height to -20% (use --H in cqw), linear and infinite; sway uses the separate rotate property, and flicker is opacity steps(6). concepts.name: Aatish Baazi (Baraat Fireworks Monogram)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A night sky. Three rockets streak up from the bottom with sparkling trails.
0.8-2.4s: Fireworks burst in gold, red and green on a dhol-like rhythm; the sparks fly out, droop with gravity and fade.
2.4-3.2s: A final big burst forms a heart, then its sparks regroup into the couple's initials.
3.2-4.2s: The initials glow, then the sparks rain down and land along the card's border as it draws itself, and the card appears.
concepts.why_it_wins: Fireworks greet the baraat at Pakistani weddings, and the moment the sparks spell the couple's initials is a genuine wow.
concepts.build_notes: key 'aatish', T0 3.8, DEF {b:'double', n:'letter', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Each burst: a gravity group (translateY droop, ease-in) contains 24-36 wrappers, each statically rotated to --ang. Inside each wrapper a spark dot translates outward (translateY 0 → -var(--R), ease-out) and fades, with a short linear-gradient tail along its axis. This composes correctly without offset-path. Initials: once document.fonts.ready resolves at setup, draw the initials onto an offscreen canvas, sample about 220 filled pixels, and store them as --tx/--ty per particle. The particles then tween from the heart positions to those targets. Rockets: dots moving up with a fading gradient tail. Sync: put burst times on a beat grid (e.g. every 0.55s, about 110 BPM). Cap the total at about 300 particles for 4K speed.

concepts.name: Truck Art Tailgate (Phool Patti Panel)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: A full-colour truck-art tailgate panel slides up from the bottom: chevrons, roses, a pair of peacocks, chamak-patti reflective strips, and swinging chains with ghungroo bells. Sign-painter lettering reads 'Shaadi Mubarak' and 'Hamza ♥ Ayesha'.
1.2-2.6s: The chains and tassels swing, the mirror strips flash in sequence, and a painted banner flaps.
2.6-3.6s: The tailgate hinges down from its bottom edge like a real truck's, revealing the card behind it with a truck-art border.
3.6-4.2s: Painted flowers pop onto the card corners.
concepts.why_it_wins: Iconic Pakistani pop art that is proud, loud, joyful and instantly Instagrammable. Truck art has gone global (Haider Ali, fashion campaigns), so it feels both desi and cool.
concepts.build_notes: key 'truck', T0 3.8, DEF {b:'truck' (new), n:'slide', d:'slide', f:'none', lan:false, spk:true}. Panel: a flat SVG built from bold shapes with thick dark outlines (stroke var(--ink), paint-order stroke). It has chevron bands, reused rose and peacock <symbol>s, and mirror strips as small polygons. Mirror flash: a white overlay on each strip with opacity keyframes staggered 80 ms; this is cheaper than a filter. Chains: rows of small ellipses swaying via rotate, with ghungroo circles. Lettering: Lalezar or Jomhuria for Urdu, Rozha One or Bungee for Latin. Tailgate drop: rotateX(0→95deg) with transform-origin bottom in a parent with perspective:180cqw, ease-in with a bounce at the end. The colour count is high, so derive the extra colours from the roles with color-mix instead of hard-coding them.

concepts.name: Ajrak Thappa (Block-Print Stamping)
storyboard: 0.0-0.4s: Plain off-white cotton cloth fills the frame.

0.4-2.4s: A carved wooden block (thappa) stamps across the cloth in a grid, left to right and top to bottom. Each stamp leaves an Ajrak star medallion in crimson and indigo, with slight ink irregularity.
2.4-3.2s: With the pattern complete, a larger block stamps the couple's initials into the central medallion.
3.2-4.2s: The cloth folds away diagonally like a shawl being draped, revealing the card, while Ajrak bands remain at the top and bottom.
concepts.why_it_wins: Ajrak is Sindh's pride and is presented to guests at weddings as a mark of respect, so Sindhi families love seeing it. The stamping rhythm syncs perfectly with dhol.
concepts.build_notes: key 'ajrak', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'ajrak' (new), n:'fade', d:'up', f:'none', lan:false, spk:false}. Pattern cell: one SVG <symbol> (an 8-fold star medallion, crimson fill, indigo ground, white dot outlines), laid out by <use> in a 5×9 grid. Stamp: the block div descends (scale 1.15→1 plus translateY) on each grid position, with JS-computed delays in 70 ms steps. On impact, the matching cell's opacity goes 0→1 with a scale 1.03→1 ink squash. Irregularity: a static displacement filter (feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap, scale 1.5) on the pattern layer. Diagonal fold: an overlay clip-path polygon animates from the full rectangle to a triangle in the top-left corner, with a darker 'back of cloth' triangle following the fold line (the classic page-curl approximation).

concepts.name: Zardozi Silai (Gold Embroidery on Velvet)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: A deep velvet backdrop with a soft nap sheen.
0.6-2.6s: A gold needle travels across the velvet, stitching a Mughal paisley-and-vine motif in gold thread, while sequins and seed pearls pop on at intervals.
2.6-3.4s: The embroidery completes into a frame around a central oval. The needle exits and light glints along the thread.
3.4-4.2s: The central oval opens out, revealing the card, and the embroidered frame settles as its border.
concepts.why_it_wins: It echoes the handwork on the bridal lehenga, so it feels couture. A needle that leaves gold thread behind it is hypnotic to watch.
concepts.build_notes: key 'zardozi', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'corner', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Thread: a dashed 'stitch' path (stroke-dasharray 1.2 .6 in user units) revealed by a mask that draws the same path with pathLength=1 + drawK, so the dash pattern stays intact while the reveal advances. Needle: offset-path: path(<same d>) with offset-distance 0→100% on the same timing and offset-rotate: auto, inside a fixed 360×640 motion box. Sequins: circles with a gold radial gradient that pop at preset path percentages; pearls are white circles with a highlight. Velvet: a radial-gradient (fl centre → darker edge) plus 4% static noise for nap. Oval opening: .card clip-path ellipse grows from (20% 14%) to (120% 120%).

concepts.name: Mehrab Corridor (Arch Arcade Fly-Through)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A view down a long arcade of cusped Mughal arches receding into soft light, like the Badshahi Mosque's arcades, with a lantern hanging in each arch.
1.0-3.4s: The camera glides forward. Each arch grows and passes overhead, revealing the next; the lanterns swing and rose petals drift toward the camera.
3.4-4.2s: The last arch ahead holds the illuminated card. The camera arrives and that arch becomes exactly the card's arch border.
concepts.why_it_wins: Very simple to build yet deeply cinematic. It works with any palette (white marble for Nikah, red sandstone for Baraat) and lands seamlessly on the arch border.
concepts.build_notes: key 'mehrab', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'arch', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:true, spk:false}. Six copies of one arch-frame SVG (an evenodd path forming a wall with a multifoil arch hole, plus inlay lines in var(--ef)), stacked with --k = 0..5. Each layer animates scale from 0.55^k to 0.55^(k-6), so layer k passes the camera in turn, with roughly linear timing and opacity fading to 0 above scale 3. Delays are equal, so the motion is continuous; transform-origin 50% 46%. Interior shading: each deeper layer is darker by color-mix(…, #000 k*8%). The light at the end is a radial-gradient of #FFE2A8. The last layer's arch path is the .b-arch path, so the hand-off is pixel-aligned. Lanterns reuse the existing lantern SVG with the sw sway.

concepts.name: Sitaron ki Baraat (Constellation Couple)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A deep night sky; stars twinkle into view and a crescent hangs at the top.
1.0-2.4s: Lines connect chosen stars to draw two minimalist constellations: a groom with a sehra on the left and a bride in a dupatta on the right (or simply their initials).
2.4-3.2s: A shooting star streaks from groom to bride, and its trail curls into a heart.
3.2-4.2s: The camera drifts into the heart, the stars soften into gold dust, and the card fades in.
concepts.why_it_wins: 'Written in the stars' (qismat) is a romantic idea in Urdu poetry. The look is minimal and elegant, and it suits dark-mode cards perfectly.
concepts.build_notes: key 'sitare', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'single', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. Background stars: seeded dots with twK infinite. Constellations: predefined point lists in a 100×178 viewBox (one for each figure), or points generated from the initials by sampling a canvas at setup. Lines are a polyline with pathLength=1 + drawK, and the nodes pop with popK. Shooting star: a small bright dot with a linear-gradient tail, moved by translate along 2 keyframes; the heart is a path drawn right after it (drawK). concepts.name: Sheesh Mahal (Mirror-Mosaic Light Wave)
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A dark chamber; a single candle flame appears at bottom-centre.
1.0-2.4s: Light ripples outward across a full-screen mosaic of hundreds of tiny convex mirror chips set in floral patterns. Each chip flashes as the wave passes, and flowers emerge in light.
2.4-3.2s: The whole ceiling glows, and a central mirror medallion shows the initials.
3.2-4.2s: The mosaic pieces fly outward toward the camera and fade, revealing the card; the edge pieces stay as a glittering border.
concepts.why_it_wins: Lahore Fort's Palace of Mirrors is legendary. A ripple of light through thousands of mirrors is pure glamour and stands apart from every other opening.
concepts.build_notes: key 'sheesh', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'double', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'dust', lan:false, spk:true}. JS builds about 400 small polygons (triangles, diamonds, hexagons) in one SVG on a floral mask grid, giving each a --dist from the flame (setup only). Flash: a fill-opacity keyframe 0.25→1→0.55 with delay dist*1.2ms (the light wave), plus an opacity flash on a white highlight polygon per chip. Gold seams: the same grid drawn again as a stroke-only copy in var(--acc). Shatter: each chip translates outward along (x-cx, y-cy), normalised × 70cqw, with rotate, scale 1.8 and opacity → 0. Delay by inverse distance so the centre goes first; edge chips (dist above a threshold) stay. Candle: a teardrop flame with a small scaleY steps flicker. Keep it to one SVG of simple polygons; 400 elements animate fine at 4K.

concepts.name: Choori Portal (Glass-Bangle Ripple)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: Rainbow glass bangles roll in from both sides, bounce gently against each other, and stack concentrically at the centre.
1.2-2.4s: The stack spins in alternating directions with glints running around each bangle; the intro line appears inside the smallest ring.
2.4-3.8s: The bangles expand outward one after another like ripples, each passing the camera, revealing the card at the centre.
3.8-4.0s: t0 at 3.6s. The last ring fades out at the edges as the text begins.
concepts.why_it_wins: Bangles are the sound and colour of mehndi night. The ripple portal is playful and joyous, quick to read and great with music.

Shine: a second circle in white at 50% with stroke-dasharray .12 .88 (pathLength=1) and a looping dashoffset, giving a moving glint. concepts.name: Doli Aayi (Rukhsati Palanquin)
storyboard: 0.0-1.5s: Dusk with string lights. A decorated doli (palanquin) with red-and-gold drapes and floral strands glides in from the left, bobbing gently. Its carrying poles run off the frame, so no bearers are shown. Petals are tossed from above.
1.5-2.5s: The doli stops at the centre and its floral curtain flutters in a soft pause.
2.5-4.0s: The front curtains gather to both sides, warm light glows from inside, and the camera pushes into the opening, which becomes the card.
4.0-4.4s: t0 at 4.0s. Petals settle on the card's garland border.
concepts.why_it_wins: The rukhsati is the emotional peak of a Pakistani wedding, and 'doli' is a much-loved image in songs and poetry. Showing only the doli, without bearers, keeps it elegant and easy to animate.
concepts.build_notes: key 'doli', T0 4.0, DEF {b:'garland', n:'hand', d:'up', f:'petal', lan:true, spk:true}. Doli: a flat SVG (a domed roof with a kalgi finial, four posts, drapes in var(--fl) with acc borders, floral strands in ef/fl) on two horizontal poles that run off-screen. Travel: translateX -120%→0 with ease-out. Bob: a separate translate on an inner wrapper, a 0.5s ease-in-out alternate loop with a finite iteration count so it stops on arrival. Curtains: two drape paths scaling scaleX(1→.2) toward their posts (transform-origin at each post). Push-in: the doli group scales 1→6 at the opening with ease-in, then cross-fades to the card. The background string lights reuse the 'ghar' light layer.

concepts.name: Sheesha Card (Clear Acrylic Invite)
storyboard: 0.0-1.2s: A clear acrylic panel slides in at a 3D angle over soft terrazzo; its bevelled edges glow with refracted light.
1.2-2.4s: The panel turns to face the camera. The printed text and a gold-foil monogram resolve on the glass, and its shadow casts faint coloured caustics on the surface.
2.4-3.4s: A light sweep travels across the glass and the panel settles.
3.4-4.2s: t0 at 3.4s. The details print in line by line.
concepts.why_it_wins: Acrylic invitations, often sent in velvet boxes, are the current luxury trend. The transparent look is modern and unlike any paper reveal.
concepts.build_notes: key 'acrylic', T0 3.4, DEF {b:'none', n:'fade', d:'up', f:'none', lan:false, spk:false}. The panel is the .card itself: cd at 70% alpha (color-mix(in srgb, var(--cd) 70%, transparent)) over a terrazzo background (seeded chips of fl/lf/acc on bg). Add a 0.6cqw inner border of linear-gradient white→transparent for the bevel, and a skewed white gradient band for the sweep (translateX, mix-blend-mode: screen). Entry: rotateY(-35deg) rotateX(12deg) plus translate → none inside a perspective parent. Cross-fade the text in only after the rotation ends, keeping text out of 3D. Caustics: two blurred rainbow-gradient ellipses offset as the shadow (static blur, rendered once). Keep the text in ink on the light terrazzo, because white text needs a darker background behind the glass.

1.8-2.8s: The camera pushes in toward the ring until the band's circle frames the screen.

concepts.name: Sunehri Qalam (Golden Calligraphy Brush Strokes)

concepts.build_notes: key 'qalam', T0 3.6, DEF {b:'none', n:'hand', d:'wipe', f:'none', lan:false, spk:false}. Strokes: three wide SVG paths (stroke-width 30-40 user units, round caps, gold gradient) drawn with pathLength=1 + drawK. The same paths sit inside an SVG <mask> on the card, so the card appears exactly where the strokes pass. Dry-brush edges: one static feTurbulence displacement filter on the stroke group.
