3.2-4.0s: The bride's name ('Ayesha') pops beneath, with 'Dulhan · دلہن'.
4.0-4.8s: A calligraphic '&' or a heart pops between them. The badges nudge closer, a mini confetti burst goes off, and 'are getting married' types on.
4.8-5.4s: Everything zooms into the heart and fades, handing off to the chosen opening.
motifs: faceless dulhan icon (lehenga, dupatta, tikka, jhoomar, nath)
concepts.why_it_wins: This is the client's own idea, and it matches what caricature-invite sellers charge for. It is personal and joyful, shows at once who is getting married, and the faceless icons suit Muslim families who avoid depicting faces.
concepts.build_notes: key 'pop', P0 5.4. Layer .pre-l (z 9, opaque bg) fades out over its last 0.4s. Spring easing: linear(0, 1.12 45%, .96 65%, 1.02 82%, 1) (Chromium 113+). Badges: 34cqw circles with a gold-gradient ring (stroke) and an inner tint of the outfit colour. Icons are flat SVGs (viewBox 0 0 100 120). Groom: a head circle (skin tone --sk, 3 tones in the UI); a pagri dome with diagonal fold stripes in var(--acc) and a teardrop kalgi; 9 sehra strands (stroke-dasharray dots, each swaying via rotate); a sherwani trapezoid in var(--ink2) or var(--lf) with buttons. Bride: a head circle; a dupatta arc in var(--fl) with a scalloped acc gota edge; tikka, jhoomar and nath as small acc shapes that twinkle; a lehenga flare with 3 border bands. No eyes or mouth. Order: if the bride's family is hosting (Baraat/Rukhsati) run the bride first; for the Walima (groom's family) run the groom first, read from a 'Whose side?' option. Name text comes from the existing name inputs: letter-by-letter is fine for Latin, but Urdu uses a whole-word right-to-left wipe.
concepts.palette_idea: Uses the active sample palette: badge ring in acc, groom outfit in ink2 or lf, bride outfit in fl, background bg with it text. Baraat: Royal Ruby. Walima: Ivory Blush. Mehndi: Marigold, with the groom in a white kurta and green shawl and the bride in yellow and green.

concepts.name: Jharokha Duet (Couple in Palace Windows)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: A palace facade with two jharokha balconies, shutters closed, and the intro line 'Two families, one celebration'.
0.6-1.6s: The left jharokha's shutters open to frame the faceless groom icon, and his name unfurls on a banner hanging below.
1.6-2.6s: The right jharokha opens to show the bride icon, and her name unfurls on her banner.
2.6-3.4s: A marigold-and-rose garland swings across between the two balconies, and a heart lantern lights up in the middle.
3.4-4.2s: The camera pushes into the heart lantern, handing off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: A more regal, architectural version of the client's 'groom then bride' sequence that reads like a royal announcement.
concepts.build_notes: key 'jharokha', P0 4.2. The facade is a flat SVG; the shutters rotate ±105deg on Y in small perspective parents. Banners unroll top→bottom with a clip-path inset, as in 'farman'. The garland morphs from straight to sagging via the CSS d property, with the bead dasharray. Reuse the Pop Story couple icons, and follow the same 'Whose side?' ordering.
concepts.palette_idea: Baraat · Red Sandstone; Walima · Marble Gold (see the opening palettes); garland in fl and acc.

concepts.name: Split-Screen Couple (Two Sides Meet)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: The screen splits diagonally. The groom's half, in his sherwani colour, slides in from the top-left with his name and 'Son of Mr & Mrs …'.
0.8-1.6s: The bride's half, in her lehenga colour, slides in from the bottom-right with her name and parents.
1.6-2.4s: The diagonal seam glows, and a calligraphic '&' medallion spins in once and locks at the centre.
2.4-3.2s: The two halves slide apart along the seam, opening onto the next scene.
concepts.why_it_wins: Modern, graphic and respectful to both families: each side's parents are named, which matters in Pakistani etiquette.
concepts.build_notes: key 'split', P0 3.2. Two full-stage divs with clip-path polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 0 100%) and polygon(100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 100%), translating in from opposite corners. Seam glow: a thin rotated div with an acc linear-gradient and a soft box-shadow. The '&' medallion uses ampK. Exit: translate the halves apart along the diagonal. Parents' names come from new 'Son of / Daughter of' inputs.
concepts.palette_idea: Groom half in ink2 or lf; bride half in fl; text in it; seam in acc.

concepts.name: Bismillah Calligraphy Draw
storyboard: 0.0-0.3s: A plain background with a faint gold-noise texture.
0.3-2.3s: 'بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم' draws itself slowly and smoothly in gold: the outline stroke first, then the fill floods in.
2.3-3.0s: A soft glow pulse, with a fine ornament line beneath. An optional translation fades in: 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful'.
3.0-3.6s: The calligraphy rises and scales to its place at the top of the card (or fades) as the opening begins.
concepts.why_it_wins: Pakistani cards begin with the Bismillah. Drawing it calmly sets a blessed tone and reassures religious families.
concepts.build_notes: key 'bism', P0 3.6. An SVG <text> in Amiri, Aref Ruqaa or Scheherazade New (Chromium shapes Arabic correctly in SVG text), using the existing wrK keyframes (stroke-dashoffset, then fill-opacity). Set stroke-dasharray long enough for the glyph outlines, or convert the text to a path with pathLength for precision. If you use a clip wipe, reveal right to left. Never bounce or spin the Bismillah, overlap it with petals, or put effects over it, and keep it fully visible for at least 1.5 s.
concepts.palette_idea: Gold acc on bg; translation in it.

concepts.name: Ayat-e-Mohabbat (Surah Ar-Rum 30:21)
storyboard: 0.0-0.5s: The background fades in with a very faint girih pattern.

0.5-3.5s: The verse 'وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا لِّتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً' is revealed line by line with a soft right-to-left wipe.

3.5-5.0s: The English (or Urdu) meaning fades up beneath: 'And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves, that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy.' (Ar-Rum 30:21).
5.0-5.8s: A gentle fade to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: This is the verse most quoted about marriage and is common on Pakistani cards. Families appreciate seeing it treated with dignity.
concepts.build_notes: key 'ayah', P0 5.8. Arabic in Amiri or Scheherazade New at 6cqw or more, with a generous line-height (2.0) for the diacritics. Reveal each line with clip-path from inset(0 0 0 100%) to inset(0), a right-to-left wipe, ease-in-out 0.9s per line. Verify the Arabic against quran.com/30/21 before shipping. Hold it still for 2 s after it completes, with no effects over the text.
concepts.palette_idea: Calm palettes: Sage Nikah or Midnight Gold. Arabic in ink2 or acc, translation in it.

concepts.name: Qubool Hai (Nikah Acceptance)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: A soft ivory background under a delicate floral arch.
0.6-1.4s: 'قبول ہے · Qubool hai' writes itself in calligraphy at the centre.
1.4-2.2s: A second, slightly smaller 'Qubool hai' writes itself above-left.
2.2-3.0s: A third appears above-right, completing a triangle, and a soft heartbeat glow passes through all three.
3.0-4.0s: 'Alhamdulillah' appears beneath, and the three phrases gently converge into a gold ring around the couple's initials.
4.0-4.6s: Hand-off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: The three acceptances are the heart of the Nikah ceremony, making this a lovely, specific and emotional intro for Nikah-only invites.
concepts.build_notes: key 'qubool', P0 4.6. Urdu text in Gulzar or Noto Nastaliq Urdu. Reveal each phrase with a right-to-left clip wipe, never per-letter spans, which break Nastaliq joining. Convergence: each phrase translates to the centre while scaling to .4 and fading, as the ring draws (drawK). Offer it only for Nikah events and keep it optional, since some families feel it should follow rather than precede the Nikah.
concepts.palette_idea: Sage Nikah or Ivory Blush; text in ink, ring in acc.

concepts.name: Save-the-Date Calendar Flip
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A desk calendar with a spiral binding drops in and settles.
0.8-2.0s: Pages flip quickly from the top through 3-4 months to the wedding month.
2.0-3.0s: A hand-drawn red-gold heart circles the wedding date, and a small 'Shaadi!' sticker pops on.
3.0-3.8s: The camera zooms into the circled date, which becomes a circle wipe into the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: It puts the date, the one thing guests must remember, front and centre, which is exactly what effective save-the-date videos do.
concepts.build_notes: key 'cal', P0 3.8. At setup, JS builds the real month grid from the date input (a 7-column CSS grid, with weekday labels in English or Urdu). Flips: page divs rotate rotateX(0→-180deg) with transform-origin top in perspective:160cqw, 0.25s each. Heart circle: a path with pathLength=1 and drawK around the date cell, positioned at setup. Circle wipe: the next layer's clip-path is a circle growing from the date cell's centre.
concepts.palette_idea: Calendar paper in ef/cd, numbers in ink, heart in fl/acc.

concepts.name: Baraat Route Map (Ghar se Venue tak)
storyboard: 0.0-0.8s: A stylised illustrated city map fades in (a river, a minaret icon, parks), and two pins drop: 'Dulha ka Ghar' and the venue.
0.8-2.8s: A dotted route draws between them. A tiny decorated car, or the groom on a white horse, travels along it, with dhol icons popping along the way and tiny fireworks on arrival.
2.8-3.6s: The venue pin bounces and the venue name and baraat time pop up, then hand off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: It doubles as directions: guests see where and when in a fun way. Illustrated maps are already a popular stationery idea.
concepts.build_notes: key 'map', P0 3.6. The map is a flat SVG (generic streets, a river band, park blobs); never copy a real map service's styling or logo. Route: a path with pathLength=1 drawn via drawK, plus a dashed overlay. Vehicle: offset-path: path(<route d>) with offset-rotate: auto, inside a fixed 360×640 motion box scaled by --k. Pins: popK with a squash on landing.
concepts.palette_idea: Light map: bg in ef, roads in cd, river in an lf tint, route in acc, pins in fl.

concepts.name: Ghori Sawari (Baraat Procession)
storyboard: 0.0-0.5s: A dusk street with string lights.

0.5-3.5s: A dhol player walks in from the left beating the drum. Behind him the groom rides a white mare with a decorated saddle and sehra, with friends dancing in silhouette (bhangra arms) behind. Petals fly and small fireworks burst overhead.
3.5-4.5s: The procession reaches the centre and '<Groom> ki Baraat' lights up in marquee bulbs above. Everyone exits right, handing off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: The baraat procession is the most festive image of a Pakistani wedding and makes the groom's side proud.
concepts.build_notes: key 'ghori', P0 4.5. Side-view silhouettes only, with no faces. Walk cycles: 3-4 pose groups toggled by steps() opacity loops with a finite iteration count, so the video length stays predictable. The horse bobs via translateY steps(2). Parallax: the lights layer moves at 40% speed. Marquee bulbs blink in a staggered sequence.
concepts.palette_idea: Night Lantern or Shahi Maroon; silhouettes in color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 60%, #000); horse in ef.

concepts.name: Families ki Taraf se (Handwritten Hosts' Letter)
storyboard: 0.0-0.6s: A sheet of laid letter paper with a fountain pen resting on it.
0.6-3.0s: The pen writes line by line, its nib moving as the ink appears: 'Mr & Mrs Tariq Mahmood' / 'request the honour of your presence' / 'at the wedding of their beloved daughter'.
3.0-3.8s: A family seal stamps beside the signature, with 'Insha'Allah' in small script.
3.8-4.4s: The letter slides away, or slides into the envelope if the opening is 'env'.
concepts.why_it_wins: Pakistani cards are invitations from the parents, so leading with the hosts' names is proper etiquette and feels personal.
concepts.build_notes: key 'letter', P0 4.4. Lines in La Belle Aurore, Homemade Apple or Mrs Saint Delafield. Reveal each line with clip-path from inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0), with the pen nib translating on X in sync (same duration and easing). The seal uses popK. The hosts' names come from a new 'Hosted by' input.
concepts.palette_idea: Paper in ef, writing in ink, seal in fl.

concepts.name: Rishta Pakka (Family Chat Bubbles)
storyboard: 0.0-0.4s: A generic phone chat screen with no app branding slides up.
0.4-3.4s: Bubbles type and pop, with typing dots between them: 'Ammi: Mithai le aao!' · 'Abbu: Rishta pakka ho gaya!' · 'Phupho: Shaadi kab hai?' · 'Hamza: 12 December, Insha'Allah'.
3.4-4.2s: The last bubble zooms to fill the screen and becomes the transition.
concepts.why_it_wins: Chat-style invites are a recognised trend for fun couples, and family banter is relatable and gets shared.
concepts.build_notes: key 'chat', P0 4.2. A generic UI with no WhatsApp green, icons or logos. Bubbles pop with popK and transform-origin at their tail corner; the typing indicator is three dots with staggered, finite 'up' keyframes. Each line is an editable text field with sensible Roman Urdu defaults.
concepts.palette_idea: Avoid WhatsApp-like beige and green. Use the sample bg with cd bubbles and fl/lf tints.

concepts.name: Dhol Thaap (Dhol Beat Countdown)
storyboard: 0.0-3.0s: A dhol drum at the centre. On each beat (about every 0.55s) the drum squashes, a colourful shockwave ring expands, and a word pops: 'Dholki' · 'Mehndi' · 'Masti' · '3 · 2 · 1'.
3.0-3.6s: A final big beat bursts confetti and hands off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: Mehndi is all about the dhol; beat-synced visuals feel alive and pair perfectly with music.
concepts.build_notes: key 'dhol', P0 3.6. A 'Beat (BPM)' option sets --beat (default 0.55s) at setup, and every beat element uses delay = n × var(--beat). Drum: an SVG cylinder with zig-zag laces in fl/acc; the squash is scale(1.06,.94). Rings: circles scaling 0→3 with a fading stroke. Words pop with popK on the beats.
concepts.palette_idea: Mehndi Marigold or Bangle Carnival.

concepts.name: Polaroid Love Story
storyboard: 0.0-1.4s: A polaroid drops and pins onto a twine with a mini clip, showing a doodle: 'First met · 2023'.
1.4-2.8s: A second polaroid: 'Rishta · 2025'.
2.8-4.2s: A third: 'Nikah · 2026', with a heart doodle.
4.2-4.8s: The camera slides along the twine into the third photo, handing off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: It tells the couple's story warmly. Photos are optional, so doodles work for families who don't want pictures.
concepts.build_notes: key 'polaroid', P0 4.8. Each polaroid is a white frame div with a drop-shadow and a slight rotation; it falls with a linear() bounce and swings on its clip (a damped rotate). Use an for photos if supplied (html2mp4 waits for ), otherwise SVG doodles. The twine is a path.
concepts.palette_idea: Paper in cd, twine in acc, doodles in ink2.

concepts.name: Boarding Pass to Forever
storyboard: 0.0-1.0s: A boarding pass slides out of a slot as if being printed: 'Flight HA 1212 · Lahore → Forever'.
1.0-2.4s: The fields type in: Passengers Hamza & Ayesha · Date · Boarding (Baraat) 7:30 PM · Gate (venue).
2.4-3.2s: A laser line scans the barcode, followed by a green tick and 'Boarding confirmed'.
3.2-3.8s: The pass tears along its perforation, handing off to the opening.
concepts.why_it_wins: A playful travel theme that modern couples love, laying out the date, time and venue clearly in a fun format.
concepts.build_notes: key 'boarding', P0 3.8. Fonts: Space Mono or Courier Prime, plus Libre Barcode 128 Text. The slide-out is a translateY with steps-like printer jitter. Typing uses width steps or per-character spans (Latin only). The scan line is a gradient bar translating across. The tear is two halves rotating and translating apart. Avoid real airline names and logos.
concepts.palette_idea: Ticket in cd with ink text; header strip in ink2; accents in acc.

concepts.name: Couple Portrait Badge (Faceless Dulha & Dulhan)
storyboard: t0+0.0-0.6s: A round or arch-shaped badge with a gold ring draws itself at the top of the card.
t0+0.6-1.2s: The faceless couple (groom left, bride right) fade and scale in; the dupatta edge and sehra strands sway gently on a loop.
Hold: every 4 s a glint passes over the bride's jewellery.
concepts.why_it_wins: It personalises the card without photos, and the outfit colours can match what the couple will actually wear.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-couple'. Reuse the icons from the Pop Story prelude and add 'Outfit colour' pickers for groom and bride (defaults: ink2 or lf for the groom, fl for the bride). Size it 22-26cqw tall at the top, under the Bismillah, and push the .in content down via a class on .st. The sway is an infinite rotate on the strand groups. A 'No figures' toggle swaps it for a monogram for conservative families.
concepts.palette_idea: Groom in ink2 or lf, bride in fl, ring in acc; selectable skin tone.

concepts.name: Jhumka Drops
storyboard: t0+0.4-1.2s: Two gold jhumka earrings drop on fine chains from the top corners of the card, bouncing slightly.
Hold: they swing like pendulums, with the pearl drops lagging behind (secondary motion) and a glint every 3 s.
concepts.why_it_wins: Jewellery is central to the Pakistani bridal look. Swinging jhumkas bring the still card to life without distracting from the text.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-jhumka'. An SVG jhumka: a dome bell with rows of filigree and 5 pearl drops. The outer group rotates ±6deg (sw keyframes); the pearls sit in an inner group rotating ±4deg with a 0.15s phase lag for secondary motion. Gold gradient. They take the slots the lanterns (.ln) use.
concepts.palette_idea: Gold in acc; pearls #F7F2E8; small stones in fl/lf.

concepts.name: Lahore Skyline Footer
storyboard: t0+1.0-2.0s: A silhouette strip rises from the bottom edge: the Badshahi Mosque's domes and minarets, Minar-e-Pakistan, and a Lahore Fort gate.
Hold: tiny window lights twinkle, with a crescent above the skyline.
concepts.why_it_wins: It anchors the card to Lahore, a point of pride for Lahori families and diaspora guests alike.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-skyline'. One SVG path about 18% of the card height, filled with color-mix(in srgb, var(--ink) 85%, var(--cd)), rising via translateY(100%→0). Window lights: 20 seeded dots with twK. When this is on, hide the bottom closing line or move it up.
concepts.palette_idea: Silhouette in ink at 85%; lights in acc.

concepts.name: Postage-Stamp Portraits & Postmark
storyboard: t0+0.6-1.4s: Two perforated postage stamps slide in from left and right, tilted toward each other, showing the faceless groom and bride.
t0+1.4-1.8s: A circular postmark, 'LAHORE · 12 DEC 2026', thuds on across both stamps with an ink texture.
concepts.why_it_wins: Inspired by a much-praised wedding suite in which stamp portraits of the couple face each other. Charming, witty and very giftable.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-stamps'. The perforated stamp edge is a repeating radial-gradient mask: radial-gradient(circle at 0.6cqw 0.6cqw, transparent .45cqw, #000 .5cqw), with the portrait inside. Postmark: an SVG circle of text on a textPath, plus wavy cancellation lines; it lands with popK and rotate(-12deg).
concepts.palette_idea: Stamp paper in cd, frames in fl/lf, postmark in ink2 at 80%.

concepts.name: Jhalar Pearl Fringe Header
storyboard: t0+0.2-1.0s: Strings of pearls and tiny flowers drop from the card's top edge like a stage jhalar or sehra, parting around the Bismillah.
Hold: the strands sway softly in a wave travelling outward from the centre.
concepts.why_it_wins: It echoes stage décor and the groom's sehra, framing the top of the card festively at a glance.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-jhalar'. 20 short strands of stroke-dasharray dot beads, with a staggered drop (translateY) and an infinite sway (rotate ±3deg, phased by index). The middle strands are shorter so the Bismillah stays clear.
concepts.palette_idea: Pearls #F7F2E8, beads in acc, flowers in fl.

concepts.name: Monogram Crest (Cypress & Roses)
storyboard: t0+0.3-1.3s: A gold crest draws itself: two cypress trees flank a cusped arch, roses curl up its sides, and the couple's initials sit inside.
Hold: a glint crosses the crest every 4 s.
concepts.why_it_wins: It gives the couple a personal emblem they can reuse on social posts. The cypress is the Mughal symbol of eternity.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-crest'. SVG paths with pathLength=1 and drawK; the initials come from .xm1/.xm2. The glint is a moving gradient on a clipped copy of the crest.
concepts.palette_idea: Lines in acc, roses in fl, cypress in lf.

concepts.name: Barakallah Du'a Ribbon
storyboard: t0+0.2-1.0s: A slim ribbon cartouche unfurls under the Bismillah, carrying the Prophetic du'a for newlyweds: 'بارك الله لكما وبارك عليكما وجمع بينكما في خير'.
Hold: static, with no effects over it.
concepts.why_it_wins: Many families like a blessing on the card. This one is dignified and small enough not to crowd the names.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-dua'. A ribbon path with folded ends; text in Amiri at 4cqw, revealed with a right-to-left clip wipe. When it is on, mask a band out of the .fall layer so petals and sparkles never cross it.
concepts.palette_idea: Ribbon in ef with acc edges; text in ink2.

concepts.name: RSVP & Location Panel
storyboard: t0+2.6-3.2s: A compact panel slides up at the bottom with RSVP names and phone numbers, a pulsing map-pin icon with the venue's short address, and an optional static QR code.
Hold: the pin pulses gently; the QR code never moves.
concepts.why_it_wins: Pakistani cards list RSVP contacts, and a QR code to the venue's location saves countless 'location bhejo' messages.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-rsvp'. A panel with a 0.5cqw acc border; RSVP lines come from inputs. Generate the QR at setup with a tiny inline QR library or a pre-rendered SVG. Make it at least 26cqw with a quiet zone of at least 2 modules, keep it static, and mask it out of the effect layers.
concepts.palette_idea: Panel in cd with ink text; pin in fl.

concepts.name: Mehndi Thaal Candle Glow
storyboard: t0+0.8-1.6s: A brass mehndi thaal slides up at the bottom of the card, holding a green henna mound, flowers and lit candles.
Hold: the candle flames flicker and a warm glow pulses.
concepts.why_it_wins: Girls dancing in with the decorated mehndi thaal and its candles is a signature moment of a Pakistani mehndi.
concepts.build_notes: key 'orn-thaal'. An SVG thaal (an ellipse with an engraved rim pattern) holding a henna mound in lf and flowers in fl/acc. Flames are teardrops with infinite scaleY and opacity steps flicker; the glow is a radial-gradient circle with an opacity pulse. Draw candles, not diyas, to keep the imagery Pakistani-Muslim.
concepts.palette_idea: Brass in acc, mound in lf, flowers in fl, flame #FFC46B.

concepts.name: Parchin Kari (Pietra Dura Vine Border)
storyboard: t0-0.4 → t0+0.2s: A white-marble frame (a 0.9cqw band with a gold inner rule) fades in around the card.

t0+0.2 → t0+1.6s: An inlaid vine grows clockwise along the frame from the top centre, and at each node a five-petal flower clicks into place in carnelian, lapis and jade inlay with fine gold outlines.
Hold: every 5 s a soft sheen passes along the marble.
concepts.why_it_wins: Taj-style stone inlay is the most refined Mughal ornament. It adds luxury while keeping the card light and airy, ideal for a daytime Walima or a Nikah.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-parchin. The frame is one SVG rect path stroked in var(--ef) for marble, with a static vein texture (feTurbulence + feColorMatrix producing grey veins at 10%). Vine: one perimeter path with pathLength=1 and drawK. Flowers are <use> elements placed at path percentages computed at setup with getPointAtLength, with popK delays that match the draw progress. Inlay colours: fl (carnelian), ink2 (lapis), lf (jade); outlines in acc.
concepts.palette_idea: Best with Marble Gold, Sage Nikah or Ivory Blush.

concepts.name: Kashi Tile Border
storyboard: t0-0.3 → t0+1.4s: 28 square tiles flip into place clockwise around the card edge, 50 ms apart: cobalt, turquoise, ochre and white floral tiles.
Hold: a glaze highlight runs around the border every 6 s.
concepts.why_it_wins: It frames the card in Lahori tilework with a fresh blue palette, and pairs with the Kashi Kari opening for a seamless hand-off.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-kashi. Reuse the tile data-URIs from the 'kashi' opening. Compute perimeter positions at setup (8 across, 14 down, at 12.5cqw). The flip is rotateY(90deg→0); the highlight is a gradient band moving along each side in sequence (infinite, with an idle segment in its keyframes).
concepts.palette_idea: Kashi Blue or Turquoise Multan.

concepts.name: Truck Art Border
storyboard: t0-0.2 → t0+0.8s: Bold chevron bands wipe in along all four sides, and painted roses bloom in each corner.
t0+0.8 → t0+1.6s: Chamak-patti strips flash in a chasing sequence; small chains with ghungroo bells hang from the top corners and swing.
Hold: the mirror chase repeats every 3 s.
concepts.why_it_wins: It turns any card into a loud, proud and fun truck-art celebration.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-truck. Four strip divs, each with repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, var(--fl) 0 1.4cqw, var(--acc) 0 2.8cqw, var(--lf) 0 4.2cqw, var(--ink2) 0 5.6cqw) and a dark 0.4cqw outline. Corners use a rose <symbol>. Mirror strips are small polygons with a white overlay whose opacity flashes on staggered delays. The chains reuse the jhumka sway.
concepts.palette_idea: Truck Art Pop or Bangle Carnival.

concepts.name: Phulkari Bagh Border
storyboard: t0-0.2 → t0+1.8s: A deep-red band with khaddar texture appears, and geometric phulkari motifs (diamonds, stars) are stitched around the frame row by row in satin darning stitches of golden yellow, orange and pink.
concepts.why_it_wins: Phulkari 'bagh' pieces were traditionally embroidered by grandmothers for a granddaughter's wedding, which makes this deeply Punjabi and emotional.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-phulkari. The motif is an SVG pattern of short parallel strokes (stitches) arranged into diamonds. Reveal it clockwise with a conic mask: @property --p (angle) inside conic-gradient(from 0deg at 50% 50%, #000 var(--p), transparent 0), animating 0→360deg. For stitch sheen, alternate stroke colours and vary the angles slightly.
concepts.palette_idea: Band color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 70%, #000); threads #F2B705, #F57C00, #E91E63 (or acc/fl tints).

concepts.name: Ajrak Band Border
storyboard: t0-0.2 → t0+1.2s: Bands of Ajrak pattern stamp in across the top and bottom, block by block from left to right, with rows of white dots between the bands.
Hold: static.
concepts.why_it_wins: A respectful nod to Sindhi heritage that pairs with the Ajrak Thappa opening.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-ajrak. Reuse the Ajrak cell <symbol> in bands of 8 cells, with 70 ms stamp delays (scale 1.04→1 plus opacity).
concepts.palette_idea: Ajrak Indigo.

concepts.name: Gota Kinari Lace
storyboard: t0-0.3 → t0+0.9s: A gold gota ribbon with a scalloped edge runs around the card (a clockwise clip reveal).
Hold: a bright shine travels around the ribbon every 4 s, and tiny sequins wink.
concepts.why_it_wins: Gota is the shimmering trim on every Pakistani bridal and mehndi outfit, so it reads as festive at once.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-gota. The border is 4 divs with gold-striped linear-gradient backgrounds (#8C6A2B, #F3D98A, #B8913F) and a repeating radial-gradient mask for the scallops on the inner edge. The shine is a moving gradient band clipped to the ribbon (infinite, with an idle segment in its keyframes). Sequins are small dots with twK.
concepts.palette_idea: Gold gota on Royal Ruby, Velvet Maroon or Ivory Blush.

concepts.name: Mughal Hashiya Margin
storyboard: t0-0.4 → t0+0.6s: Inner rules draw around the text panel: thin gold, then lapis, then gold again.
t0+0.6 → t0+1.6s: The outer margin fills with a gold floral scroll on a salmon or pistachio ground, fading in from the corners.
concepts.why_it_wins: It makes the card look like an illuminated Mughal album page: scholarly, elegant and distinctive.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-hashiya. Nested rect strokes with pathLength=1 and drawK. The margin ground is solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 30%, #fff) or color-mix(in srgb, var(--lf) 30%, #fff). The floral scroll is an SVG pattern in acc at 70%, revealed from the corners outward by a radial mask. Keep the vines bird-free and figure-free.
concepts.palette_idea: Ivory Blush (salmon ground) or Pistachio Walima (pistachio ground), with ink2 lapis rules.

concepts.name: Moti Mala Arch (Pearl-Strung Arch)
storyboard: t0-0.3 → t0+1.2s: Pearls bead along the arch outline one by one, rising from the base up both sides to meet at the apex.
t0+1.2 → t0+1.6s: Teardrop pearl drops fall into place at intervals and swing.
Hold: the drops swing gently.
concepts.why_it_wins: Pearls read as bridal and pure, and the beading animation is delicate and satisfying.
concepts.build_notes: class bd-moti. The arch path is stroked with stroke-dasharray 0 2.2 and round caps, which renders as dots. A mask path drawn with drawK reveals it in two halves, base to apex. The drops are <use> elements at computed points, swaying with sw.
concepts.palette_idea: Pearls #F7F2E8 with acc highlights on any dark palette, or ink2-tinted pearls on light palettes.

concepts.name: Girih Star Lattice
storyboard: From frame 1: the lattice sits static at 8-12% opacity behind the intro and at 5-7% on the card.
From t0+1s: a wide, soft band of light drifts diagonally across the pattern every 6 s, making it shimmer.
concepts.why_it_wins: A quiet Islamic texture that adds richness without competing with the text.
concepts.build_notes: pt-girih. An SVG <pattern> built from one star-and-cross tile path. Shimmer: a second copy in var(--acc) at 30%, masked by a moving linear-gradient (@property --g), infinite with an idle segment.
concepts.palette_idea: acc on bg/cd at low opacity.

concepts.name: Mughal Jaal Trellis
storyboard: An ogee trellis with a small buti flower in each cell, tone-on-tone, drifting in a slow 2% parallax during the hold.
concepts.why_it_wins: The classic Mughal textile and architecture lattice, elegant on dark velvet or ivory.
concepts.build_notes: pt-jaal. An SVG pattern: the ogee is two mirrored S-curves, plus a 5-petal buti. The drift translates the pattern layer 0→-2cqw with infinite alternate timing; a finite 10 s drift would lengthen the render.
concepts.palette_idea: color-mix(in srgb, var(--acc) 40%, var(--bg)) on bg; ink2 at 6% on cd.

concepts.name: Kairi Paisley Damask
storyboard: A tone-on-tone paisley (buta) damask at 7%. A foil glint sweeps across it once at t0+1.5s and then every 7 s.
concepts.why_it_wins: Paisley is the most beloved subcontinental textile motif and reads as bridal fabric.
concepts.build_notes: pt-paisley. An SVG pattern of the paisley motif, with the glint done the same way as the girih lattice shimmer.
concepts.palette_idea: fl or acc tone-on-tone.

concepts.name: Jamawar Brocade Shimmer
storyboard: A woven brocade field of small floral medallions in gold thread. A band of light passes over it so the threads glint, as if the fabric were turning in the light.
concepts.why_it_wins: Jamawar and kimkhab brocades are heirloom wedding fabrics, so this feels luxurious and tactile.
concepts.build_notes: pt-brocade. Draw the pattern twice: a base in color-mix(in srgb, var(--bg) 94%, #fff), and a gold-thread copy in acc masked by a moving gradient. Add 0.15cqw weave lines via a repeating-linear-gradient at 4% for a fabric feel.
concepts.palette_idea: Velvet Maroon, Emerald Darbar or Royal Ruby.

concepts.name: Multani Blue Florals
storyboard: Hand-painted-style blue and turquoise florals on white at 10%, static. Optionally, a large central rosette rotates slowly (0.5°/s) behind the intro.
concepts.why_it_wins: Multan's blue pottery is a famous Pakistani craft, and the pattern feels fresh and cool for daytime events.
concepts.build_notes: pt-multani. An SVG pattern of a 6-petal flower with leaves in ink2 and lf; the rosette layer has an infinite linear spin.
concepts.palette_idea: Turquoise Multan or Kashi Blue.

concepts.name: Starry Night
storyboard: Seeded stars twinkle across the background, and about every 5 s a shooting star streaks across the top third.
concepts.why_it_wins: Night-sky romance that pairs with the Chaand, Sitare and Fanoos openings.
concepts.build_notes: pt-stars. 60 seeded dots with twK (infinite). The shooting star is an infinite animation whose keyframes stay idle from 0-90% and streak from 90-100%.
concepts.palette_idea: Stars #FFFFFF/#FFE7A8 on Midnight Gold, Dusk Lahore or Cosmic Navy.

concepts.name: Jugnu (Fireflies)
storyboard: From t0: 20-25 soft glowing dots drift on looping curved paths, pulsing brighter and dimmer. A few drift in front of the card edges, never over the names.
concepts.why_it_wins: Magical, subtle life on the held card.
concepts.build_notes: f:'jugnu'. Each firefly is an outer div translating on X (ease-in-out alternate, 6-11 s) and an inner div translating on Y with a different duration, giving Lissajous paths. The glow is a radial-gradient dot with mix-blend-mode: screen and an opacity pulse. Seeded positions keep them within the outer 18% margins.
concepts.palette_idea: #FFE9A3 glow on dark palettes; acc on light palettes.

concepts.name: Gulab Pashi (Rose-Petal Burst)
storyboard: t0-0.2s: About 40 rose petals burst from the top edge, as if thrown by family at the baraat.
t0 → t0+3s: The petals flutter down, tumbling in 3D, then thin out to 8-10 slowly falling petals for the hold.
concepts.why_it_wins: Gulab pashi is THE baraat welcome, and 3D tumbling petals look far richer than flat confetti.
concepts.build_notes: f:'gulab'. Each petal is a curved SVG shape with an fl gradient. The fall uses translate keyframes; the tumble is rotateX plus rotateY animations on an inner element, with a slightly darker second layer for the back face. The burst petals are finite and end by t0+3s; the hold petals loop infinitely.
concepts.palette_idea: fl with color-mix(in srgb, var(--fl) 70%, #000) for the back face.

concepts.name: Sone ki Chamak (Foil Glint on Names)
storyboard: At t0+2.5s and then every 4 s, a specular band of light sweeps across the names, the ampersand and the event title, as if the gold foil caught the light.
concepts.why_it_wins: A real foil glint is what makes gold look like gold rather than yellow.
concepts.build_notes: fx-glint. HTML names and the event title use background-clip:text with a gold gradient at background-size 300%, animating background-position (infinite, with idle keyframes). For SVG handwriting names, CSS cannot animate gradientTransform and SMIL isn't seekable, so overlay a copy of the text whose <mask> contains a gradient <rect>, and animate that rect's CSS transform.
concepts.palette_idea: Gold stops #8C6A2B/#E9CF7A/#FFF4C8/#B8913F.

concepts.name: Bokeh & Light Leak
storyboard: t0-0.5 → t0+1s: A warm light leak (an amber→rose gradient) sweeps diagonally across once.
Hold: 12 soft bokeh discs drift slowly behind the card frame (screen blend).
concepts.why_it_wins: It gives a cinematic, filmed-on-camera warmth.
concepts.build_notes: fx-bokeh. The light leak is a large gradient div, pre-blurred via radial-gradients, translating once. The bokeh are seeded discs with soft radial-gradient edges on an infinite drift. Optional photo: the Unsplash bokeh photo-1512320265221 as an at 30%.
concepts.palette_idea: Leak #FFB86B→#FF7A8A; bokeh in acc/fl tints.

concepts.name: Phuljhari (Sparkler-Written Names)
storyboard: t0+0.7s: A sparkler tip writes the bride's name in glowing gold, spraying sparks from the moving tip; the written line cools from white-hot to gold.
t0+1.6s: The same happens for the groom's name.
concepts.why_it_wins: Phuljhari sparklers are part of every mehndi and baraat night, and names written in fire are a wow.
concepts.build_notes: n:'sparkler'. Build on the existing 'hand' names mode (SVG text stroke draw). The emitter is a small group on offset-path along a hand-authored baseline path that follows the writing direction (left→right). It emits 3-4 spark particles per 0.1s at seeded angles, all finite. Glow: a duplicate of the text with a static feGaussianBlur that fades out. The stroke colour animates #FFFFFF→acc.
concepts.palette_idea: Dark palettes: Firework Night, Night Lantern.

concepts.name: Mehndi Cone Piping (Henna-Piped Names)
storyboard: t0+0.7s: The names are piped on in thick henna paste (rounded, slightly raised strokes), with a cone tip moving ahead of the line.
t0+2.5s: The paste 'dries', and its colour shifts from fresh green-brown to deep maroon-orange.
concepts.why_it_wins: It turns the names into mehndi itself, the perfect detail for a mehndi invite.
concepts.build_notes: n:'henna'. SVG text stroke draw with stroke-width about 2.2 user units, stroke-linecap round and paint-order stroke; the fill fades in last. The drying is a CSS stroke colour animation from #5B4A1E to #8A2E12. The cone is a small triangle translating on X in sync with the draw.
concepts.palette_idea: Mehndi Marigold, Basant Sky.

concepts.name: Bakhoor Smoke Mist
storyboard: From t0: soft wisps of smoke curl up from the bottom corners and dissolve near the middle, on very slow 8-12 s loops.
concepts.why_it_wins: It evokes oud and bakhoor, a luxe Arabian-Islamic mood that suits a Nikah.
concepts.build_notes: f:'oud'. 5-6 large pre-blurred blobs (radial-gradient, no live filter) with infinite translate, scale and rotate, at opacity ≤ .18. Use mix-blend-mode: screen on dark palettes and a multiply-tinted version on light ones.
concepts.palette_idea: Smoke color-mix(in srgb, var(--it) 60%, transparent).

concepts.name: Gota Confetti Burst
storyboard: t0-0.1s: Shiny ribbon confetti (gold, pink and green strips, plus sequins) bursts from both lower corners in arcs.
t0 → t0+2.5s: The strips flip and flutter in 3D as they fall and fade.
concepts.why_it_wins: It gives the reveal instant celebration energy.
concepts.build_notes: fx-confetti. 40 strips. Each arc uses nested wrappers with separate X and Y easings; an inner element spins with rotateX and rotateY. All finite, in acc/fl/lf.
concepts.palette_idea: acc, fl, lf.

concepts.name: Genda Phool Rain (Marigold)
storyboard: From t0: marigold petals and a few whole marigold heads fall and spin, thickest at the start and gentle during the hold.
concepts.why_it_wins: Marigold garlands and petals are the colour of mehndi and mayun décor in Pakistan.
concepts.build_notes: f:'genda'. A variant of the existing .fall system. Petals are small ruffled orange and yellow SVG circles that rotate; whole flowers are 3 rings of scalloped circles.

concepts.name: Living Card (Camera Drift & Parallax Hold)
storyboard: From t0+2s to te: the whole card very slowly pushes in (scale 1→1.035) while the border and background pattern drift the opposite way by 0.6cqw, so the final hold feels filmed rather than frozen.
concepts.why_it_wins: Top templates never freeze. A subtle Ken Burns drift keeps the 6-8 s hold alive without moving the text block relative to itself.
concepts.build_notes: fx-drift. Apply it to a wrapper inside .card, not to .card itself, which the openings animate. Use scale and translate in one linear animation lasting (te - t0 - 2) s, so it ends exactly at te and doesn't extend the render.
concepts.palette_idea: n/a

concepts.name: Bilingual Urdu-English Card
storyboard: t0+0.0s: The Arabic Bismillah fades in, followed by the line 'نحمده ونصلي على رسوله الكريم'.
t0+0.6s: The names appear in Urdu Nastaliq at the top with a right-to-left wipe, e.g. 'عائشہ ❀ حمزہ'.
t0+1.4s: The English names appear beneath in script, and the event title shows in both languages ('بارات · Baraat').
t0+2.2s: The details appear in two mirrored columns (Urdu on the right, English on the left), with the closing line in Roman Urdu.
concepts.why_it_wins: Bilingual Urdu-English cards are a top Pakistani trend, and they let both grandparents and young guests read comfortably.
concepts.build_notes: ly-bi. Urdu blocks use dir='rtl' with Gulzar or Noto Nastaliq Urdu at a line-height of at least 2 for Nastaliq descenders. Never split Urdu into letter spans, which breaks the joining; use right-to-left clip-path wipes. A two-column mirrored grid. Add Urdu fields for the names, event and venue, with transliteration defaults.
concepts.palette_idea: Any palette; Urdu in ink2, English in ink.

concepts.name: Programme Timeline
storyboard: t0+2.0 → t0+3.4s: A vertical timeline draws down the lower half, and four stops pop in one by one with tiny icons: Baraat arrival 7:30 PM (horse), Nikah 8:00 PM (rings and pen), Dinner 9:30 PM (plate), Rukhsati 11:00 PM (doli).
concepts.why_it_wins: Pakistani cards commonly list the programme timings, and guests love knowing when dinner is served.
concepts.build_notes: ly-program. The vertical line draws with drawK and the stops pop with popK. The icons are small SVG symbols in acc. Times come from new inputs. The Walima version uses Arrival, Dinner and Photo session.
concepts.palette_idea: Line and icons in acc; times in ink2.

concepts.name: Three-Event Itinerary
storyboard: t0+1.8 → t0+3.6s: Three small cusped arches slide up side by side (or stacked): Mehndi in green and yellow, Baraat in red and gold, Walima in ivory and gold, each with its date, time and venue. The current event's arch is larger and glows.
concepts.why_it_wins: One shareable video covers the whole shaadi week, so families don't have to send three separate invites.
concepts.build_notes: ly-events. Each arch is a mini-card using the matching event palette from the sample, staggered 0.25s. The current event is highlighted with scale 1.08 and an acc glow.
concepts.palette_idea: Mehndi: Marigold tints; Baraat: Royal Ruby tints; Walima: Ivory Blush tints.

concepts.name: Muntazir & RSVP Footer
storyboard: t0+2.8 → t0+3.6s: A slim footer fades in: 'Muntazir' followed by relatives' names in two columns, 'RSVP' with two phone numbers, and an optional 'Dua-go' line.
concepts.why_it_wins: This is proper Pakistani card etiquette: families expect to see the hosts and the RSVP names.
concepts.build_notes: ly-muntazir. Text at 3.6-4cqw, with the Urdu headings in Nastaliq. Content comes from a textarea, one name per line. The panel is masked out of the effect layers.
concepts.palette_idea: Headings in ink2; names in ink.

concepts.name: Story Pages (Instagram-Story Card)
storyboard: t0: Progress bars appear at the top, in three segments.
t0 → t0+3s: Page 1 shows the Bismillah, the couple badge and the names.
t0+3 → t0+6s: Page 2 slides in from the right with the event, date, time and venue.
t0+6 → t0+9s: Page 3 shows the RSVP, map pin and closing line.
concepts.why_it_wins: It feels native to Instagram and WhatsApp stories and fits more information without cramming.
concepts.build_notes: ly-story. Three page containers move in with translateX keyframes and delays, and the progress bars fill via scaleX 0→1 per segment (finite). The total length grows by about 3 s, so raise --te accordingly. Keep the last page up for at least 4 s.
concepts.palette_idea: Progress bars in it at 60%; pages in cd.

concepts.name: Minimal Monogram Modern
storyboard: t0 → t0+1s: A large monogram of the initials fades up in a thin serif within a hairline circle.
t0+1 → t0+2.5s: The names appear in small caps with generous tracking, then the event and date beneath, and thin rules draw in.
concepts.why_it_wins: Modern couples want quiet luxury, and a minimal layout reads cleanly even at thumbnail size.
concepts.build_notes: ly-minimal. Fonts: Italiana or Cinzel for the monogram, Cormorant for the text. Keep lots of negative space and strokes of at least 0.25cqw to avoid shimmer in video.
concepts.palette_idea: Cotton Foil, Terrazzo Clear, Lilac Silver.
